title.zh: 卷二百零 列傳第一百二十五 儒學下
title.raw: 卷二百零 列傳第一百二十五 儒學下 Volume 200 Biographies 125: Confucian Scholars 3

sentences.zh: 儒學下

translations.literal: Confucian Learning, Part Three
translations.idiomatic: Confucian Scholars, Part Three

sentences.zh: 褚無量

translations.literal: Chu Wuliang
translations.idiomatic: Chu Wuliang

sentences.zh: 褚無量，字弘度，杭州鹽官人。

translations.literal: Chu Wuliang, courtesy name Hongdu, was a man of Yanguan in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Wuliang, whose courtesy name was Hongdu, came from Yanguan in Hangzhou Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼授經於沈子正、曹福，刻意墳典。

translations.literal: In youth he received the classics from Shen Zizheng and Cao Fu, and applied himself strenuously to the ancient texts.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he studied the classics under Shen Zizheng and Cao Fu, devoting himself single-mindedly to the canon of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 家濱臨平湖，有龍出，人皆走觀，無量尚幼，讀書若不聞，眾異之。

translations.literal: His family lived on the shore of Linping Lake. When a dragon appeared, everyone ran to watch, but Wuliang was still young and kept reading as though he had heard nothing; the crowd marveled at this.
translations.idiomatic: His family lived beside Linping Lake. When a dragon emerged, all the neighbors rushed out to look, yet Wuliang, still a child, continued reading as if he heard nothing at all. Everyone found this remarkable.

sentences.zh: 尤精《禮》、司馬《史記》。

translations.literal: He was especially accomplished in the Rites and in Sima Qian's Records of the Grand Historian.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially steeped in the Rites and in Sima Qian's Records of the Grand Historian.

sentences.zh: 擢明經第，累除國子博士，遷司業兼修文館學士。

translations.literal: He placed in the Mingjing examination, was repeatedly appointed Guozi boshi, and was promoted to siye while concurrently serving as a Xiuwen Guan academician.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination, rose through successive appointments as Doctor of the National University, and was promoted to Vice Director of Education while also serving as an academician of the Hall for Cultivating Literature.

sentences.zh: 中宗將南郊，詔定儀典。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong was about to perform the southern suburban sacrifice, an edict ordered that the ritual code be fixed.
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Zhongzong prepared to offer sacrifice at the southern suburb, he issued an edict requiring the rites to be defined.

sentences.zh: 時祝欽明、郭山惲建言皇后為亞獻，無量與太常博士唐紹、蔣欽緒固爭，以為：「郊祀，國大事，其折衷莫如《周禮》。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Qinming and Guo Shanyun proposed that the empress serve as the secondary offering official. Wuliang, together with the Taichang doctors Tang Shao and Jiang Qinxu, firmly contested this, arguing: "The suburban sacrifice is a great affair of state; for settling it there is nothing better than the Rites of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhu Qinming and Guo Shanyun urged that the empress serve as the secondary offering official. Wuliang, along with the Masters of Rites Tang Shao and Jiang Qinxu, objected strenuously, holding that the suburban sacrifice was a matter of paramount state importance and that no authority could settle it better than the Rites of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》冬至祭天圓丘，不以地配，唯始祖為主，亦不以妣配，故後不得與。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou say that at the winter solstice Heaven is sacrificed to at the Round Mound; Earth is not paired with it, only the founding ancestor serves as the principal spirit, and no consort is paired either; therefore the empress may not participate.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Rites of Zhou, Heaven is sacrificed to at the Round Mound on the winter solstice without pairing Earth with the rite; only the founding ancestor serves as the principal recipient, and no consort is paired with him either. The empress therefore cannot take part.

sentences.zh: 又《大宗伯》：『凡大祭祀，王後不與，則攝而薦豆籩，徹。』

translations.literal: Moreover, the Grand Master of Ceremonies states: "In any great sacrifice, if the queen does not participate, she then acts in proxy, presenting the dishes and trays and withdrawing them."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Grand Master of Ceremonies says: "Whenever the queen does not join a major sacrifice, she stands in proxy to present the dishes and trays and to withdraw them afterward."

sentences.zh: 是後不應助祭。

translations.literal: Thus the empress should not assist in the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that the empress should not assist in the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 又內宰職『大祭祀，後祼獻則贊瑤爵。』

translations.literal: Again, the duties of the Palace Steward state: "In a great sacrifice, when the empress performs the libation offering, she assists by presenting the jade goblet."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Steward's duties likewise state: "At a great sacrifice, when the empress performs the libation offering, she assists by presenting the jade goblet."

sentences.zh: 祭天無祼，知此乃宗廟祭耳。

translations.literal: There is no libation in sacrifices to Heaven; from this one knows that this refers only to ancestral temple sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Since sacrifices to Heaven involve no libation, this passage clearly refers to ancestral temple rites alone.

sentences.zh: 巾車、內司服，掌後六服與五路，無後祭天之服與路，是後不助祭天也。

translations.literal: The Master of Chariots and the Palace Mistress of Attire manage the empress's six ceremonial robes and five chariots; there are no robes or chariots for the empress in sacrifices to Heaven; thus the empress does not assist in sacrifices to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Chariots and the Palace Mistress of Attire oversee the empress's six ceremonial robes and five chariots, yet no robes or chariots are assigned to the empress for sacrifices to Heaven. The empress therefore does not assist in heavenly sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 惟漢有天地合祭，皇后參享事。

translations.literal: Only under the Han were Heaven and Earth sacrificed to together, and the empress took part in the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Only under the Han dynasty were Heaven and Earth sacrificed to together, with the empress sharing in the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 末代黷神，事不經見，不可為法。」

translations.literal: In the final age the spirits were profaned; such practices are not found in the canonical texts and cannot serve as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In decadent times the spirits were profaned; such practices have no warrant in the classics and cannot be taken as precedent.

sentences.zh: 時左僕射韋巨源佐欽明，故無量議格。

translations.literal: At that time the Left Vice Director Wei Juyuan supported Qinming, and so Wuliang's proposal was rejected.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Wei Juyuan sided with Qinming at the time, and Wuliang's proposal was set aside.

sentences.zh: 以母老解官。

translations.literal: He resigned his office because his mother was old.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned from office to care for his aged mother.

sentences.zh: 開元五年，帝將幸東都而太廟壞，姚崇建言：「廟本苻堅故殿，不宜罷行。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan, the emperor was about to visit the Eastern Capital when the Imperial Ancestral Temple collapsed. Yao Chong proposed: "The temple was originally Fu Jian's old hall; the journey should not be canceled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan, the emperor planned to visit the Eastern Capital, but the Imperial Ancestral Temple fell into ruin. Yao Chong urged: "The temple stands on what was once Fu Jian's old palace hall; the journey ought not to be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 無量鄙其言，以為不足聽，乃上疏曰：「王者陰盛陽微，則先祖見變。

translations.literal: Wuliang despised these words and considered them unworthy of heed. He submitted a memorial saying: "When a ruler's yin is excessive and yang insufficient, the ancestors manifest signs of change.
translations.idiomatic: Wuliang held this advice in contempt and deemed it unworthy of attention. He submitted a memorial stating: "When a ruler's yin grows excessive and yang grows weak, the ancestors reveal signs of change.

sentences.zh: 今後宮非禦幸者，宜悉出之，以應變異。

translations.literal: Now all palace women who are not favored by the emperor should be sent out entirely, in response to these portents.
translations.idiomatic: All consorts in the inner palace who no longer receive the emperor's favor should be dismissed, so as to answer these omens.

sentences.zh: 舉畯良，撙奢靡，輕賦，慎刑，納諫爭，察諂諛，繼絕世，則天人和會，災異訖息。」

translations.literal: Promote the worthy and good, restrain extravagance, lighten taxes, apply punishments with caution, accept remonstrance, scrutinize flattery, and continue extinct lineages—then Heaven and humanity will harmonize and calamities and portents will cease."
translations.idiomatic: Promote the worthy, curb extravagance, lighten taxes, punish with restraint, heed remonstrance, expose flattery, and revive lineages cut off in their prime—then Heaven and humanity will be in accord and calamities will cease."

sentences.zh: 帝是崇語，車駕遂東。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed with Chong's words, and the imperial carriage proceeded east.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sided with Yao Chong, and the imperial procession set out for the east.

sentences.zh: 無量又上言：「昔虞舜之狩，秩山川，遍群神。

translations.literal: Wuliang submitted another memorial: "In antiquity, when Yu Shun went on hunting tours, he ordered the mountains and rivers and visited all the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Wuliang submitted another memorial: "In antiquity, when Emperor Shun went on royal hunts, he ranked the mountains and rivers in order and paid homage to all the spirits.

sentences.zh: 漢孝景祠黃帝橋山，孝武祠舜九疑，高祖過魏祭信陵君墓，過趙封樂毅後，孝章祠桓譚冢。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing of Han sacrificed to the Yellow Emperor at Qiaoshan; Emperor Wu sacrificed to Shun at Jiuyi; Emperor Gaozu, passing through Wei, sacrificed at the tomb of Lord Xinling; passing through Zhao, he enfeoffed a descendant of Yue Yi; Emperor Zhang sacrificed at the tomb of Huan Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing of Han sacrificed to the Yellow Emperor at Mount Qiao; Emperor Wu sacrificed to Shun at Jiuyi; Emperor Gaozu, passing through Wei, offered sacrifice at the tomb of Lord Xinling, and passing through Zhao enfeoffed a descendant of Yue Yi; Emperor Zhang sacrificed at the tomb of Huan Tan.

sentences.zh: 願陛下所過名山、大川、丘陵、墳衍，古帝王、賢臣在祀典者，並詔致祭。

translations.literal: I wish that wherever Your Majesty passes—famous mountains, great rivers, hills, mounds, and plains—and wherever ancient emperors and worthy ministers are listed in the sacrificial canon, edicts be issued to perform sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that wherever Your Majesty passes—renowned mountains, great rivers, hills, mounds, and plains—and wherever ancient emperors and worthy ministers appear in the sacrificial canon, edicts be issued commanding sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 自古受命之君，必興滅繼絕，崇德報功。

translations.literal: From antiquity, rulers who received the Mandate have necessarily revived what was extinguished and continued what was cut off, honoring virtue and rewarding merit.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, every ruler who received the Mandate has revived what was extinguished and continued what was cut off, honoring virtue and repaying merit.

sentences.zh: 故存人之國，大於救人之災；

translations.literal: Thus preserving a person's state is greater than rescuing a person from disaster;
translations.idiomatic: Thus to preserve a man's patrimony is a greater act than to rescue him from disaster;

sentences.zh: 立人之後，重於封人之墓。

translations.literal: establishing a person's heir is weightier than enfeoffing a person's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: and to establish a man's heir weighs more than merely honoring his tomb.

sentences.zh: 願到東都，收敘唐初逮今功臣世絕者，雖在支庶，鹹得承襲。」

translations.literal: I wish that upon reaching the Eastern Capital, Your Majesty gather and record meritorious ministers from the beginning of Tang until now whose lineages have died out; even if they are collateral or common branches, all may inherit.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that upon reaching the Eastern Capital, Your Majesty trace and restore the lineages of meritorious ministers from the founding of Tang down to the present whose families have died out, so that even collateral branches may inherit their titles.

sentences.zh: 帝納其言，即詔無量祠堯平陽，宋璟祠舜蒲阪，蘇颋祠禹安邑，在所刺史參獻。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his words and immediately issued edicts: Wuliang was to sacrifice to Yao at Pingyang, Song Jing to Shun at Puban, and Su Ting to Yu at Anyi; the local prefects were to join in the offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice and at once ordered Wuliang to sacrifice to Yao at Pingyang, Song Jing to Shun at Puban, and Su Ting to Yu at Anyi, with the local prefects joining in the offerings.

sentences.zh: 又求武德以來勛臣苗裔，紹續其封。

translations.literal: He also sought descendants of meritorious ministers since the Wude era and restored their enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: He also searched out descendants of meritorious ministers since the Wude reign and restored their hereditary titles.

sentences.zh: 初，內府舊書，自高宗時藏宮中，甲乙叢倒，無量建請繕錄補第，以廣秘籍。

translations.literal: Initially the old books of the inner treasury, stored in the palace since Emperor Gaozong's time, were jumbled and disordered in their classifications. Wuliang proposed that they be repaired, copied, and re-cataloged to expand the collection of secret texts.
translations.idiomatic: At first the old books of the imperial treasury, housed in the palace since Gaozong's reign, lay in chaotic disorder by category. Wuliang proposed that they be repaired, recopied, and re-cataloged to enlarge the collection of rare texts.

sentences.zh: 天子詔於東都乾元殿東廂部匯整比，無量為之使。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven issued an edict that in the eastern wing of Qianyuan Hall at the Eastern Capital the books be gathered, sorted, and collated, with Wuliang appointed commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the books gathered, sorted, and collated in the eastern wing of Qianyuan Hall at the Eastern Capital, with Wuliang appointed to oversee the work.

sentences.zh: 因表聞喜尉盧僎、江夏尉陸去泰、左監門率府胄曹參軍王擇從、武陟尉徐楚璧分部讎定。

translations.literal: He thereupon memorialized recommending Wenxi Assistant Magistrate Lu Zhen, Jiangxia Assistant Magistrate Lu Qutai, Left Directorate of Palace Gates Commandant's Office Registrar Wang Zecong, and Wuzhi Assistant Magistrate Xu Chubi to divide the work of collation and verification.
translations.idiomatic: He then recommended Wenxi Assistant Magistrate Lu Zhen, Jiangxia Assistant Magistrate Lu Qutai, Registrar Wang Zecong of the Left Directorate of Palace Gates, and Wuzhi Assistant Magistrate Xu Chubi to divide the work of collation and verification.

sentences.zh: 衛尉設次，光祿給食。

translations.literal: The Minister of Guards set up quarters, and the Minister of Imperial Household provided food.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Guards provided quarters, and the Minister of Imperial Household supplied meals.

sentences.zh: 又詔秘書省、司經局、昭文、崇文二館更相檢讎，采天下遺書以益闕文。

translations.literal: An edict was also issued ordering the Secretariat, the Office of Classics, and the Zhaowen and Chongwen academies to cross-check one another's work and collect lost books from throughout the realm to supplement missing passages.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered the Secretariat, the Office of Classics, and the Zhaowen and Chongwen academies to cross-check one another's work and gather lost books from across the realm to fill gaps in the texts.

sentences.zh: 不數年，四庫完治。

translations.literal: Within a few years the four repositories were fully completed.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the four libraries were fully restored.

sentences.zh: 帝詔群臣觀書，賜無量等帛有差。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the ministers to view the books and bestowed silk on Wuliang and the others in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned the ministers to view the books and bestowed silk rewards of varying measure upon Wuliang and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 無量又言：「貞觀禦書皆宰相署尾，臣位卑不足以辱，請與宰相聯名跋尾。」

translations.literal: Wuliang also said: "During Zhenguan all imperial books were signed at the end by chancellors. My rank is too low to bear such an honor; I request to co-sign the colophon with a chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Wuliang also said: "During the Zhenguan era every imperial book bore a chancellor's signature at the end. My rank is too low for such an honor; I ask permission to co-sign the colophon with a chancellor.

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: This was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 帝西還，徙書麗正殿，更以脩書學士為麗正殿直學士，比京官預朝會。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned west, the books were moved to Lizheng Hall; the title of book-editing academician was changed to Lizheng Hall Direct Academician, with status comparable to capital officials who attended court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned west, the books were moved to Lizheng Hall, the book-editing academicians were renamed Direct Academicians of Lizheng Hall, and they were granted standing comparable to capital officials who attended court.

sentences.zh: 復詔無量就麗正纂續前功。

translations.literal: An edict was again issued ordering Wuliang to continue the previous work of compilation at Lizheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again ordered Wuliang to continue the earlier compilation at Lizheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 皇太子及四王未就學，無量以《孝經》、《論語》五通獻帝。

translations.literal: The crown prince and four princes had not yet begun their studies; Wuliang presented the emperor with five copies each of the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince and four princes had not yet begun their schooling; Wuliang presented the emperor with five copies each of the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕知之矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I understand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I take your meaning.

sentences.zh: 乃選郗常亨、郭謙光、潘元祚等為太子、諸王侍讀。

translations.literal: He then selected Xi Changheng, Guo Qianguang, Pan Yuanzuo, and others as attendant readers for the crown prince and the princes.
translations.idiomatic: He then selected Xi Changheng, Guo Qianguang, Pan Yuanzuo, and others to serve as reading tutors to the crown prince and the princes.

sentences.zh: 七年，太子齒胄於學，詔無量升坐講勸，百官觀禮，厚賚賜。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the crown prince performed the capping ceremony at the school; an edict ordered Wuliang to ascend and lecture in encouragement; the officials observed the rite, and generous rewards were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the crown prince came of age at the National University; the emperor ordered Wuliang to ascend the lectern and deliver an exhortation, with officials of all ranks in attendance, and generous rewards were granted.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 病困語人，以麗正書未畢為恨。

translations.literal: In his illness he told others that his regret was that the Lizheng books were not yet finished.
translations.idiomatic: On his sickbed he told those around him that his greatest regret was that the Lizheng library project remained unfinished.

sentences.zh: 帝聞悼痛，詔宰相曰：「無量，朕師，今其永逝，宜用優典。」

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he mourned in grief and issued an edict to the chancellors: "Wuliang was my teacher; now that he has departed forever, exceptional honors should be used.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard the news he grieved deeply and told the chancellors: "Wuliang was my teacher; now that he is gone forever, he should receive the highest honors.

sentences.zh: 於是贈禮部尚書，謚曰文，葬事官給。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was posthumously made Minister of Rites, given the posthumous name Wen, and his funeral expenses were supplied by the state.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites, given the posthumous name Wen, and his funeral was provided for by the state.

sentences.zh: 所撰述百餘篇。

translations.literal: Works he composed numbered more than a hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He authored more than a hundred works.

sentences.zh: 歿後有於書殿得講《史記》、《至言》十二篇上之，帝嘆息，以絹五百匹賜其家。

translations.literal: After his death twelve chapters of his lectures on the Records of the Grand Historian and Utmost Words were found in a book hall and submitted; the emperor sighed and bestowed five hundred bolts of silk on his family.
translations.idiomatic: After his death twelve chapters of his lectures on the Records of the Grand Historian and Utmost Words were discovered in a book hall and presented to the throne; the emperor sighed in admiration and bestowed five hundred bolts of silk on his family.

sentences.zh: 始，無量與馬懷素為侍讀，後秘書少監康子原、國子博士侯行果亦踐其選，雖賞賚亟加，而禮遇衰矣。

translations.literal: At first Wuliang and Ma Huaisu served as attendant readers; later the Secretariat Vice Director Kang Ziyuan and the Guozi doctor Hou Xingguo also entered this selection. Although rewards were frequently increased, the courtesy shown them declined.
translations.idiomatic: At first Wuliang and Ma Huaisu served as imperial reading tutors; later Secretariat Vice Director Kang Ziyuan and National University Doctor Hou Xingguo joined their ranks. Rewards grew ever more frequent, but the respect accorded them waned.

sentences.zh: 陸去泰，歷左右補闕內供奉。

translations.literal: Lu Qutai successively served as Left and Right Remonstrance Official and Inner Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qutai served in succession as Left and Right Remonstrance Official and as an Inner Attendant.

sentences.zh: 王擇從，京兆人，終汜水令。

translations.literal: Wang Zecong was a man of Jingzhao and ended as magistrate of Sishui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zecong, a native of Jingzhao, ended his career as magistrate of Sishui.

sentences.zh: 徐安貞

translations.literal: Xu Anzhen
translations.idiomatic: Xu Anzhen

sentences.zh: 徐楚璧，初應制舉，三登甲科，開元時為中書舍人、集賢院學士，帝屬文多令視草。

translations.literal: Xu Chubi, at first responding to the imperial examination, thrice placed in the top grade. During Kaiyuan he served as Secretariat Drafter and Jixian Academy academician; the emperor often entrusted him with reviewing drafts.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chubi first entered the imperial examination and three times placed in the top grade. During the Kaiyuan era he served as Secretariat Drafter and academician of the Jixian Academy; the emperor often entrusted him with reviewing draft edicts.

sentences.zh: 終中書侍郎，東海縣子。

translations.literal: He ended as Vice Director of the Secretariat and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Donghai County.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Vice Director of the Secretariat and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Donghai County.

sentences.zh: 在中書省久，是時李林甫用事，或言計議多所參助。

translations.literal: He served long in the Secretariat; at that time Li Linfu held power, and some said he often took part in and assisted in deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: He served for many years in the Secretariat. Li Linfu was then in power, and some said Xu often took part in his deliberations.

sentences.zh: 後更名安貞。

translations.literal: Later he changed his name to Anzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He later changed his name to Anzhen.

sentences.zh: 元行沖

translations.literal: Yuan Xingchong
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xingchong

sentences.zh: 元淡，字行沖，以字顯，後魏常山王素蓮之後。

translations.literal: Yuan Dan, courtesy name Xingchong, became known by his courtesy name; he was a descendant of Su Lian, Prince of Changshan of Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Dan, courtesy name Xingchong, was known by his courtesy name. He was a descendant of Su Lian, Prince of Changshan of Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 少孤，養於外祖司農卿韋機。

translations.literal: He lost his father young and was raised by his maternal grandfather, Minister of Revenue Wei Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he was raised by his maternal grandfather Wei Ji, Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 及長，博學，尤通故訓。

translations.literal: When he grew up he was broadly learned and especially versed in ancient glosses.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he was broadly learned and especially versed in ancient exegesis.

sentences.zh: 及進士第，累遷通事舍人。

translations.literal: Upon placing in the jinshi examination he was repeatedly promoted to Protocol Officer.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he rose through successive promotions to Protocol Officer.

sentences.zh: 狄仁傑器之。

translations.literal: Di Renjie valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂仁傑曰：「下之事上，譬富家儲積以自資也，脯臘膎胰以供滋膳，參術芝桂以防疾疢。

translations.literal: He once said to Renjie: "A subordinate serving his superior is like a wealthy household storing provisions for its own use—dried meats and cured meats to supply rich fare, ginseng, atractylodes, lingzhi, and cassia to guard against illness.
translations.idiomatic: He once told Renjie: "Serving a superior is like a wealthy household stocking provisions for its own use—cured meats to enrich the table, ginseng, atractylodes, lingzhi, and cassia to ward off illness.

sentences.zh: 門下充旨味者多矣，願以小人備一藥石，可乎？」

translations.literal: Your gate is filled with many who supply delicacies; I wish to serve as one medicinal stone for you—may I?
translations.idiomatic: Your gate already has many who supply delicacies; may I serve as one bitter remedy among them?

sentences.zh: 仁傑笑曰：「君正吾藥籠中物，不可一日無也。」

translations.literal: Renjie smiled and said: "You are precisely what belongs in my medicine chest; I cannot be without you for a single day."
translations.idiomatic: Renjie smiled and said: "You are exactly what belongs in my medicine chest—I cannot do without you for a single day."

sentences.zh: 景雲中，授太常少卿。

translations.literal: During the Jingyun era he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyun era he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 行沖以系出拓拔，恨史無編年，乃撰《魏典》三十篇，事詳文約，學者尚之。

translations.literal: Xingchong, tracing his lineage to the Tuoba, regretted that history had no chronicle; he therefore composed the Wei Canon in thirty chapters—detailed in events, concise in style—and scholars honored it.
translations.idiomatic: Xingchong, whose lineage traced to the Tuoba, lamented the lack of a chronological history of Wei and composed the Wei Canon in thirty chapters—rich in detail yet spare in style—which scholars held in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 初，魏明帝時，河西柳谷出石，有牛繼馬之象。

translations.literal: Initially, in the time of Emperor Ming of Wei, a stone emerged at Liugu in Hexi with an image of an ox following a horse.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Ming of Wei, a stone emerged at Liugu in Hexi bearing the image of an ox following a horse.

sentences.zh: 魏收以晉元帝乃牛氏子冒司馬姓，以著石符。

translations.literal: Wei Shou held that Emperor Yuan of Jin was actually a son of the Niu clan who falsely took the surname Sima, and recorded this as a stone omen.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou held that Emperor Yuan of Jin was in fact a son of the Niu clan who had falsely assumed the surname Sima, and he recorded this as fulfillment of the stone omen.

sentences.zh: 行沖謂昭成皇帝名犍，繼晉受命，獨此可以當之。

translations.literal: Xingchong said that Emperor Zhaocheng's name was Jian, that he succeeded Jin in receiving the Mandate, and that this alone could correspond to the omen.
translations.idiomatic: Xingchong argued that Emperor Zhaocheng's given name was Jian, that he received the Mandate after Jin, and that this alone fit the omen.

sentences.zh: 有人破古冢得銅器，似琵琶，身正圓，人莫能辨。

translations.literal: Someone broke open an ancient tomb and obtained a bronze vessel resembling a pipa, with a perfectly round body; no one could identify it.
translations.idiomatic: Someone opened an ancient tomb and found a bronze vessel resembling a pipa, perfectly round in body, which no one could identify.

sentences.zh: 行沖曰：「此阮鹹所作器也。」

translations.literal: Xingchong said: "This is an instrument made by Ruan Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Xingchong said: "This is an instrument made by Ruan Xian.

sentences.zh: 命易以木，弦之，其聲亮雅，樂家遂謂之「阮鹹」。

translations.literal: He ordered it reproduced in wood and strung; its sound was clear and elegant, and musicians thereafter called it the "Ruan Xian."
translations.idiomatic: He had it reproduced in wood and strung; its tone was clear and elegant, and musicians thereafter called the instrument the "Ruan Xian."

sentences.zh: 開元初，罷太子詹事，出為岐州刺史，兼關內按察使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he was removed as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and sent out as prefect of Qi Prefecture, concurrently serving as Inspector of Guannei.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era he was dismissed as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and appointed prefect of Qi Prefecture, concurrently serving as Inspector of Guannei.

sentences.zh: 自以書生，非彈治才，固辭。

translations.literal: Considering himself a mere scholar and not possessed of talent for investigation and governance, he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He considered himself a scholar without talent for investigation and governance and firmly declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 入為右散騎常侍、東都副留守。

translations.literal: He entered court as Right Attendant Cavalier and Deputy Protector of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Right Attendant Cavalier and Deputy Protector of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 嗣彭王子誌謙坐仇人告變，考訊自誣，株蔓數十人，行沖察其枉，列奏見原。

translations.literal: Prince Zhizhao, son of Prince of Peng, was implicated when an enemy reported a plot; under interrogation he falsely confessed and dozens were implicated. Xingchong found the injustice, submitted a detailed memorial, and they were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhizhao, son of the Prince of Peng, was accused by an enemy of plotting rebellion; under interrogation he falsely confessed and dozens were implicated. Xingchong found the case unjust, submitted a detailed memorial, and the victims were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 四遷大理卿，不樂法家，固謝所居官，改左散騎常侍，封常山縣公。

translations.literal: After four promotions to Minister of Justice, disliking the legalist approach he firmly declined the office he held and was changed to Left Attendant Cavalier, enfeoffed as Duke of Changshan County.
translations.idiomatic: After four promotions to Minister of Justice he disliked the legalist approach, firmly declined the post, and was reassigned as Left Attendant Cavalier and enfeoffed as Duke of Changshan County.

sentences.zh: 充使檢校集賢，再遷太子賓客、弘文館學士。

translations.literal: He served as commissioner to inspect the Jixian Academy and was twice promoted to Guest of the Heir Apparent and Hongwen Guan academician.
translations.idiomatic: He served as commissioner to inspect the Jixian Academy and was twice promoted to Guest of the Heir Apparent and academician of the Hongwen Guan.

sentences.zh: 先是，馬懷素撰書誌，褚無量校麗正四部書，業未卒，相次物故。

translations.literal: Previously Ma Huaisu had compiled a book catalogue and Chu Wuliang had collated the four divisions of books at Lizheng; the work was not finished when they died one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Ma Huaisu had compiled a book catalogue and Chu Wuliang had collated the four divisions of books at Lizheng Hall; neither task was finished before they died in succession.

sentences.zh: 詔行沖並代之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Xingchong to take over both tasks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Xingchong to take over both tasks.

sentences.zh: 玄宗自註《孝經》，詔行沖為疏，立於學官。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong personally annotated the Classic of Filial Piety and ordered Xingchong to compose a commentary, which was established in the official schools.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong personally annotated the Classic of Filial Piety and ordered Xingchong to write a commentary, which was adopted as an official school text.

sentences.zh: 以老罷麗正校書事。

translations.literal: Because of age he was relieved of the Lizheng book-collation duties.
translations.idiomatic: On account of age he was relieved of his duties collating books at Lizheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 初，魏光乘請用魏征《類禮》列於經，帝命行沖與諸儒集義作疏，將立之學，乃引國子博士範行恭、四門助教施敬本采獲刊綴為五十篇，上於官。

translations.literal: Initially Wei Guangcheng requested that Wei Zheng's Classified Rites be ranked among the classics. The emperor ordered Xingchong and the various Confucians to gather interpretations and compose commentaries, intending to establish it in the schools. He then summoned the Guozi doctor Fan Xinggong and the Simen assistant instructor Shi Jingben to collect, compile, and edit it into fifty chapters, which were submitted to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Wei Guangcheng petitioned that Wei Zheng's Classified Rites be ranked among the classics. The emperor ordered Xingchong and other Confucian scholars to gather interpretations and compose commentaries, intending to establish the text in the schools. He then had National University Doctor Fan Xinggong and Simen Assistant Instructor Shi Jingben collect and edit the material into fifty chapters, which were submitted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 於是右丞相張說建言：「戴聖所錄，向已千載，與經並立，不可罷。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Right Chancellor Zhang Yue proposed: "What Dai Sheng recorded has already stood for a thousand years alongside the classics; it cannot be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Right Chancellor Zhang Yue then urged: "The Rites compiled by Dai Sheng have stood alongside the classics for a thousand years; they cannot be set aside.

sentences.zh: 魏孫炎始因舊書擿類相比，有如鈔綴，諸儒共非之。

translations.literal: Wei Sunyan at first took the old books, extracted passages by category, and compared them, like stitched excerpts; the various Confucians jointly rejected this.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sunyan had first extracted passages by category from the old texts and stitched them together like copied excerpts, which the Confucian scholars widely rejected.

sentences.zh: 至征更加整次，乃為訓註，恐不可用。」

translations.literal: When Zheng further reorganized it and made it into exegesis and annotation, it was feared that it could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: Even when Wei Zheng further reorganized the material into commentary and annotation, it was feared the result would be unusable.

sentences.zh: 帝然之，書留中不出。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed; the book was kept within the palace and not issued.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and the book was kept within the palace and never issued.

sentences.zh: 行沖意諸儒間己，因著論自辯，名曰《釋疑》。

translations.literal: Xingchong believed the Confucians were criticizing him and therefore composed a treatise in self-defense titled Resolution of Doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Xingchong believed the other scholars were speaking against him and wrote a treatise in self-defense titled Resolution of Doubts.

sentences.zh: 曰：

translations.literal: It reads:
translations.idiomatic: It reads:

sentences.zh: 客問主人：「小戴之學，康成之註，魏氏乃有刊易，二經孰優？」

translations.literal: A guest asked the host: "The learning of Xiao Dai, the annotations of Kangcheng—yet the Wei clan made revisions and changes; which of the two classics is superior?
translations.idiomatic: A guest asked the host: "The learning of Xiao Dai and the annotations of Zheng Xuan—yet Wei Zheng dared to revise them. Which of the two classics is superior?

sentences.zh: 主人曰：「《小戴禮》行於漢末，馬融為傳，盧植合二十九篇而為之解，世所不傳。

translations.literal: The host said: "The Rites of Xiao Dai circulated at the end of Han; Ma Rong made a commentary, and Lu Zhi combined twenty-nine chapters and wrote explanations for them—these were not transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: The host replied: "The Rites of Xiao Dai circulated at the end of the Han dynasty; Ma Rong wrote a commentary on them, and Lu Zhi combined twenty-nine chapters and supplied explanations, but these were not handed down.

sentences.zh: 鉤黨獄起，康成於竄伏之中，理紛挐之典，雖存探究，咨謀靡所。

translations.literal: When the Partisan Proscription arose, Kangcheng, in hiding and flight, sorted out tangled classics; although he preserved investigation, he had no one with whom to consult.
translations.idiomatic: When the Partisan Proscription arose, Zheng Xuan, in hiding and exile, still worked to untangle the confused classics; though he pursued inquiry, he had no counselors to consult.

sentences.zh: 具《鄭志》者百有余科，章句之徒，曾不是省。

translations.literal: Those who fully recorded the Zheng Records numbered more than a hundred categories; the followers of textual glosses never once examined them.
translations.idiomatic: The Zheng Records contained more than a hundred categories of material, yet the scholars devoted to textual glosses never once examined them.

sentences.zh: 王肅因之，或多攻詆。

translations.literal: Following Wang Su's lead, many launched attacks and denunciations.
translations.idiomatic: Following Wang Su's example, many scholars launched attacks and denunciations.

sentences.zh: 而鄭學有孫炎，雖扶鄭義，條例支分，箴石間起，增革百篇。

translations.literal: Within Zheng Xuan's school there was Sun Yan, who though he upheld Zheng's doctrines subdivided provisions into branches, inserted admonitory stones here and there, and added and revised a hundred sections.
translations.idiomatic: Within Zheng Xuan's school was Sun Yan, who though he upheld Zheng's doctrines still subdivided provisions into branches, inserted admonitions throughout, and added and revised a hundred sections.

sentences.zh: 魏氏病群言之冗脞，采眾說之精簡，刊正芟礱，書畢以聞，太宗嘉賞，錄賜儲貳。

translations.literal: The Wei clan took issue with the verbose and fragmentary mass of commentaries, collected the finest and most concise of various interpretations, edited corrected pruned and polished the text, and upon completing the book reported it to the throne; Emperor Taizong praised and rewarded it and had it copied and bestowed upon the heir.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei clan objected to the verbose and fragmentary mass of commentaries, gathered the finest and most concise interpretations, edited and polished the text, and upon completing the book reported it to the throne. Emperor Taizong praised and rewarded the work and had it copied and bestowed upon the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 陛下纂業，宜所循襲，乃制諸儒，甄分舊義。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has inherited the enterprise and ought to follow in that path; thus you commanded the Confucians to sort through and distinguish the old interpretations.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has inherited the enterprise and ought to follow that precedent; you therefore commanded the Confucian scholars to sort through and distinguish the old interpretations.

sentences.zh: 豈悟章句之士，堅持昔言，擯壓不申，疑於知新，果於仍故？」

translations.literal: Who would have thought that the scholars devoted to textual glosses would cling to their old opinions, suppress and refuse to advance new views, doubt the knowing of new things, and be resolute in holding to what is old?"
translations.idiomatic: Who would have thought that scholars devoted to textual glosses would cling to their old opinions, suppress new views and refuse to speak out, doubt the value of knowing what is new, and be resolute in holding to what is old?"

sentences.zh: 客曰：「當局稱迷，傍觀必審，何所為疑而不申列？」

translations.literal: The guest said: Those within the situation call themselves confused, but the bystander must be clear—what is there to doubt that prevents you from presenting your case?
translations.idiomatic: The guest said: "Those caught up in affairs call themselves confused, but the bystander sees clearly—what is there to doubt that keeps you from presenting your case?

sentences.zh: 答曰：「改易章句，是有五難：漢孔安國註《古文尚書》，族兄臧與書曰：『相如常忿俗儒淫詞冒義，欲撥亂反正而未能也。

translations.literal: The reply came: To change textual glosses presents five difficulties. Han Kong Anguo annotated the Old Text Book of Documents, and his clansman Zang wrote to him saying: Xiangru often resented how vulgar Confucians used excessive words that obscured meaning; he wanted to restore order from chaos but could not achieve it.
translations.idiomatic: The reply came: "To change textual glosses presents five difficulties. When Kong Anguo of Han annotated the Old Text Book of Documents, his clansman Zang wrote to him: 'Xiangru often resented how vulgar Confucians used excessive words that obscured meaning; he wanted to restore order from chaos but could not achieve it.

sentences.zh: 浮學守株，眾非非正，自古而然，恐此道未信，而獨智為譴。』

translations.literal: Floating scholarship clings like a stump-waiting hare; the masses denounce what is not orthodox—this has been so since antiquity. I fear this doctrine will not be trusted, and solitary wisdom will be blamed.
translations.idiomatic: Shallow scholarship clings to the old like a hare waiting by a stump; the crowd denounces what is not orthodox—this has been so since antiquity. I fear this doctrine will not be trusted, and solitary wisdom will be condemned.

sentences.zh: 一也。

translations.literal: This is the first.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first.

sentences.zh: 昔孔季產專古學，有孔扶者與俗浮沈，每誡產曰：『今朝廷率章句內學，君獨脩古義。

translations.literal: In the past Kong Jichan devoted himself to ancient learning. There was Kong Fu, who drifted along with the vulgar currents, and always admonished Jichan saying: The court today generally favors textual glosses and inner learning; you alone cultivate ancient meaning.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Kong Jichan devoted himself to ancient learning. There was Kong Fu, who drifted with the vulgar currents and always admonished Jichan: 'The court today generally favors textual glosses and inner learning; you alone cultivate ancient meaning.

sentences.zh: 古義非章句內學，危身之道也，獨善不容於世，君其殆哉！』

translations.literal: Ancient meaning is not textual glosses and inner learning—it is a path that endangers one's person. Solitary excellence finds no place in the world—you are likely in peril!
translations.idiomatic: Ancient meaning is not textual glosses and inner learning—it is a path that endangers one's person. Solitary excellence finds no place in the world—you are likely in peril!

sentences.zh: 二也。

translations.literal: This is the second.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second.

sentences.zh: 劉歆好《左氏》，欲建學官，哀帝納之，諸儒遷延不肯置對。

translations.literal: Liu Xin favored the Zuo Tradition and wished to establish an academic chair for it. Emperor Ai accepted the proposal, but the Confucians delayed and refused to respond when questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin favored the Zuo Tradition and wished to establish an academic chair for it. Emperor Ai accepted the proposal, but the Confucian scholars delayed and refused to respond when questioned.

sentences.zh: 歆移書誚讓，諸博士皆忿恨。

translations.literal: Xin sent letters reproaching them, and all the erudites were filled with resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Xin sent letters reproaching them, and all the erudites were filled with resentment.

sentences.zh: 龔勝時為光祿大夫，見歆議，乃乞骸骨。

translations.literal: Gong Sheng, then Senior Master of the Palace, upon seeing Xin's proposal, asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Sheng, then Senior Master of the Palace, upon seeing Xin's proposal, asked to retire from office.

sentences.zh: 司空師丹因大發怒，詆歆改亂前誌，非毀先帝所立。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Shi Dan was greatly angered thereby, denouncing Xin for altering and disrupting previous records and slandering what the former emperor had established.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Shi Dan was greatly angered and denounced Xin for altering and disrupting previous records and slandering what the former emperor had established.

sentences.zh: 歆懼，出為五原太守。

translations.literal: Xin, in fear, was sent out as Administrator of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xin, in fear, was sent out as Administrator of Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 以君賓之學，公仲之博，猶迫同門朋黨之議，卒令子駿負謗。

translations.literal: With the learning of Junbin and the breadth of Gongzhong, he was still constrained by partisan disputes within the same school, and in the end caused Zijun to bear slander.
translations.idiomatic: With the learning of Junbin and the breadth of Gongzhong, he was still constrained by partisan disputes within the same school, and in the end caused Zijun to bear slander.

sentences.zh: 三也。

translations.literal: This is the third.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third.

sentences.zh: 王肅規鄭玄數千百條，鄭學馬昭詆劾肅短。

translations.literal: Wang Su cited against Zheng Xuan several thousand or even tens of thousands of passages; Ma Zhao of Zheng Xuan's school impeached Su's failings.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su cited against Zheng Xuan several thousand or even tens of thousands of passages; Ma Zhao of Zheng Xuan's school impeached Su's shortcomings.

sentences.zh: 詔遣博士張融按經問詰，融推處是非，而肅酬對疲於歲時。

translations.literal: An imperial command sent Erudite Zhang Rong to examine the classics and question them; Rong weighed right and wrong, and Su spent a full year exhausted in rebuttal.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial command sent Erudite Zhang Rong to examine the classics and question them; Rong weighed right and wrong, and Su spent an entire year exhausted in rebuttal.

sentences.zh: 四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth.

sentences.zh: 王粲曰：『世稱伊、雒以東，淮、漢以北，康成一人而已。

translations.literal: Wang Can said: The age proclaimed that east of the Yi and Luo rivers, north of the Huai and Han rivers, Kangcheng alone sufficed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Can said: 'The age proclaimed that east of the Yi and Luo rivers and north of the Huai and Han, Kangcheng alone sufficed.

sentences.zh: 鹹言先儒多闕，鄭氏道備。』

translations.literal: All said the early Confucians had many lacunae, and the Way of the Zheng clan was complete.
translations.idiomatic: All said the early Confucians had many lacunae, and the Way of the Zheng clan was complete.

sentences.zh: 粲竊嗟怪，因求所學，得《尚書註》，退思其意，意皆盡矣，所疑猶未諭焉，凡有二篇。

translations.literal: Can privately sighed in wonder; he therefore sought out what he had studied and obtained Zheng's Commentary on the Book of Documents. Reflecting on its meaning afterward, he found its intent was fully expressed, yet points of doubt still remained unclear—in all, two chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Can privately sighed in wonder; he therefore sought out what he had studied and obtained Zheng's Commentary on the Book of Documents. Reflecting on its meaning afterward, he found its intent fully expressed, yet points of doubt still remained unclear—in all, two chapters.

sentences.zh: 王邵曰：『魏、晉浮華，古道湮替，歷載三百，士大夫恥為章句。

translations.literal: Wang Shao said: Wei and Jin were frivolous and ornate; the ancient Way was submerged and lost. For three hundred years scholars and officials were ashamed to engage in textual glosses.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao said: 'Wei and Jin were frivolous and ornate; the ancient Way was submerged and lost. For three hundred years scholars and officials were ashamed to engage in textual glosses.

sentences.zh: 唯草野生專經自許，不能博究，擇從其善，徒欲父康成，兄子慎，寧道孔聖誤，諱言鄭、服非。』

translations.literal: Only rustic scholars in the wilds claimed mastery of a single classic; unable to pursue broad investigation and choose what was good, they merely wished to call Kangcheng father and Zishen elder brother—sooner say Confucius was mistaken than admit Zheng and Fu were wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Only rustic scholars in the wilds claimed mastery of a single classic; unable to pursue broad investigation and choose what was good, they merely wished to call Kangcheng father and Zishen elder brother—sooner say Confucius was mistaken than admit Zheng and Fu were wrong.

sentences.zh: 然則鄭、服之外，皆讎矣。

translations.literal: Thus apart from Zheng and Fu, all became adversaries.
translations.idiomatic: Thus apart from Zheng and Fu, all became adversaries.

sentences.zh: 五也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth.

sentences.zh: 夫物極則變，比及百年，當有明哲君子，恨不與吾同世者。

translations.literal: When things reach their extreme they change; within a hundred years there surely will be a wise and enlightened gentleman who regrets not living in the same age as I.
translations.idiomatic: When things reach their extreme they change; within a hundred years there will surely be a wise and enlightened gentleman who regrets not living in the same age as I.

sentences.zh: 道之行廢，必有其時者歟？

translations.literal: Whether the Way is practiced or abandoned must have its proper time, must it not?
translations.idiomatic: Whether the Way is practiced or abandoned must have its proper time, must it not?

sentences.zh: 何遽速近名之嫌邪？」

translations.literal: Why hasten to invite suspicion of seeking a quick name?
translations.idiomatic: Why hasten to invite suspicion of seeking a quick name?"

sentences.zh: 俄丐致仕，十七年卒，年七十七，贈禮部尚書，謚曰獻。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he requested retirement. He died in the seventeenth year, at age seventy-seven, and was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites with the posthumous title Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter he requested retirement. He died in the seventeenth year, at age seventy-seven, and was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites with the posthumous title Offered.

sentences.zh: 陳貞節

translations.literal: Chen Zhenjie
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhenjie

sentences.zh: 陳貞節，潁川人。

translations.literal: Chen Zhenjie was a native of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhenjie was a native of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 開元初，為右拾遺。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he served as Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan era he served as Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 初，隱、章懷、懿德、節湣四太子並建陵廟，分八署，置官列吏卒，四時祠官進饗。

translations.literal: Initially the four crown princes Yin, Zhanghuai, Yide, and Jiemin all had mausoleum temples built for them, divided into eight offices, with officials clerks and soldiers appointed, and sacrificial officers presenting offerings in all four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the four crown princes Yin, Zhanghuai, Yide, and Jiemin all had mausoleum temples built for them, divided into eight offices with officials, clerks, and soldiers appointed, and sacrificial officers presenting offerings in all four seasons.

sentences.zh: 貞節以為非是，上言：「王者制祀，以功德者猶親盡而毀，四太子廟皆別祖，無功於人，而園祠時薦，有司守衛，與列帝侔。

translations.literal: Zhenjie considered this improper and submitted a memorial: When a king establishes sacrifices, even those based on merit and virtue are destroyed when kinship ties are exhausted. The temples of the four crown princes are all separate ancestral shrines; they performed no service to the people, yet receive seasonal offerings in garden temples, with officials guarding them, equal to the arrayed emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenjie considered this improper and submitted a memorial: "When a king establishes sacrifices, even those based on merit and virtue are destroyed when kinship ties are exhausted. The temples of the four crown princes are all separate ancestral shrines; they performed no service to the people, yet receive seasonal offerings in garden temples with officials guarding them, on a par with the emperors.

sentences.zh: 金奏登歌，所以頌功德，《詩》曰：『鐘鼓既設，一朝饗之。』

translations.literal: Metal music and ascending songs are used to praise merit and virtue. The Odes says: The bells and drums having been set up, in one morning they are feasted.
translations.idiomatic: Metal music and ascending songs are used to praise merit and virtue. The Odes says: 'The bells and drums having been set up, in one morning they are feasted.

sentences.zh: 使無功而頌，不曰舞詠非度邪？

translations.literal: If those without merit are praised, is this not singing and dancing beyond measure?
translations.idiomatic: To praise those without merit—is this not singing and dancing beyond measure?

sentences.zh: 周制：始祖乃稱小廟。

translations.literal: Zhou institutions: only the founding ancestor is called a lesser temple.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou institutions, only the founding ancestor is called a lesser temple.

sentences.zh: 未知四廟欲何名乎？

translations.literal: It is not known what the four temples are to be called.
translations.idiomatic: It is not known what the four temples are to be called.

sentences.zh: 請罷卒吏，詔祠官無領屬，以應禮典。

translations.literal: I request that the soldiers and clerks be abolished and that sacrificial officers be commanded to have no subordinates, in accordance with ritual canon.
translations.idiomatic: I request that the soldiers and clerks be abolished and that sacrificial officers be commanded to have no subordinates, in accordance with ritual canon.

sentences.zh: 古者別子為祖，故有大、小宗。

translations.literal: In antiquity a son by a secondary wife became an ancestor, hence there were greater and lesser lineages.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity a son by a secondary wife became an ancestor, hence there were greater and lesser lineages.

sentences.zh: 若謂祀未可絕，宜許所後子孫奉之。」

translations.literal: If it is said that sacrifices cannot yet be discontinued, the descendants who succeed them should be permitted to maintain them.
translations.idiomatic: If it is said that sacrifices cannot yet be discontinued, the descendants who succeed them should be permitted to maintain them."

sentences.zh: 詔有司博議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to deliberate broadly.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the relevant offices to deliberate broadly.

sentences.zh: 駕部員外郎裴子余曰：「四太子皆先帝冢嗣，列聖念懿屬而為之享。

translations.literal: Assistant Master of Carriages Pei Ziyu said: The four crown princes were all heir sons of former emperors; the successive sages, mindful of their close kinship, established sacrifices for them.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Master of Carriages Pei Ziyu said: "The four crown princes were all heir sons of former emperors; the successive sages, mindful of their close kinship, established sacrifices for them.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》書晉世子曰：『將以晉畀秦，秦將祀予。』

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals records the Jin heir prince saying: I am about to give Jin to Qin; Qin will sacrifice to me.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals records the Jin heir prince saying: 'I am about to give Jin to Qin; Qin will sacrifice to me.

sentences.zh: 此不祀也。

translations.literal: This concerns not being sacrificed to.
translations.idiomatic: This concerns not being sacrificed to.

sentences.zh: 又言：『神不歆非類，君祀無乃戾乎！』

translations.literal: It also says: Spirits do not accept offerings from those not of their kind—would not the lord's sacrifice be perverse!
translations.idiomatic: It also says: 'Spirits do not accept offerings from those not of their kind—would not the lord's sacrifice be perverse!

sentences.zh: 此有廟也。

translations.literal: This concerns having a temple.
translations.idiomatic: This concerns having a temple.

sentences.zh: 魯定公元年，立煬宮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duke Ding of Lu, the Yang Palace was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Duke Ding of Lu, the Yang Palace was established.

sentences.zh: 煬，伯禽子，季氏遠祖，尚不為限，況天子篤親親以及旁期，誰不曰然？」

translations.literal: Yang was a son of Bo Qin, a distant ancestor of the Ji clan, and was not yet subject to limits—how much more so when the Son of Heaven deeply cherishes kinship and extends it to collateral relations—who would not say this is right?
translations.idiomatic: Yang was a son of Bo Qin, a distant ancestor of the Ji clan, and was not yet subject to limits—how much more so when the Son of Heaven deeply cherishes kinship and extends it to collateral relations—who would not say this is right?"

sentences.zh: 太常博士段同曰：「四陵廟皆天子睦親繼絕也。

translations.literal: Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Duan Tong said: The four mausoleum temples are all cases of the Son of Heaven cherishing kinship and continuing broken lines.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Duan Tong said: "The four mausoleum temples are all cases of the Son of Heaven cherishing kinship and continuing broken lines.

sentences.zh: 逝者錫蘋繁，猶生者之開茅土。

translations.literal: The departed are granted offerings of duckweed and artemisia, just as the living are granted fief domains.
translations.idiomatic: The departed are granted offerings of duckweed and artemisia, just as the living are granted fief domains.

sentences.zh: 古封建子弟，詎皆有功？

translations.literal: In antiquity enfeoffed princes and sons—did they all have merit?
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity enfeoffed princes and sons—did they all have merit?

sentences.zh: 生無所議，死乃援禮停祠，人其謂何？

translations.literal: While living there was no discussion; only after death is ritual invoked to stop sacrifices—what will people say?
translations.idiomatic: While living there was no discussion; only after death is ritual invoked to stop sacrifices—what will people say?

sentences.zh: 隱於上，伯祖也，服緦；

translations.literal: Yin was senior to the emperor—a father's elder brother's son; mourning was one year with hempen sash.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was senior to the emperor—a father's elder brother's son; mourning was one year with hempen sash.

sentences.zh: 章懷，伯父也，服期；

translations.literal: Zhanghuai was a father's elder brother; mourning was one full year.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanghuai was a father's elder brother; mourning was one full year.

sentences.zh: 懿德、節湣，堂昆弟也，服大功。

translations.literal: Yide and Jiemin were paternal cousins of the same generation; mourning was nine months.
translations.idiomatic: Yide and Jiemin were paternal cousins of the same generation; mourning was nine months.

sentences.zh: 親未盡，廟不可廢。」

translations.literal: Kinship ties are not yet exhausted; the temples cannot be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Kinship ties are not yet exhausted; the temples cannot be abolished."

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書鄭惟忠等二十七人亦附其言。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Zheng Weizhong and twenty-seven others also endorsed this view.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Zheng Weizhong and twenty-seven others also endorsed this view.

sentences.zh: 於是四陵廟惟減吏卒半，它如舊。

translations.literal: Thereupon the four mausoleum temples had only their soldiers and clerks reduced by half; everything else remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the four mausoleum temples had only their soldiers and clerks reduced by half; everything else remained as before.

sentences.zh: 遷太常博士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 玄宗奉昭成皇后祔睿宗室，又欲肅明皇后並升焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong had Empress Zhaocheng enshrined alongside Emperor Ruizong, and also wished to have Empress Suming elevated together with her.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong had Empress Zhaocheng enshrined alongside Emperor Ruizong, and also wished to have Empress Suming elevated together with her.

sentences.zh: 貞節奏言：「廟必有配，一帝一後，禮之正也。

translations.literal: Zhenjie submitted a memorial: A temple must have a consort; one emperor and one empress—this is the correct ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenjie submitted a memorial: "A temple must have a consort; one emperor and one empress—this is correct ritual.

sentences.zh: 昭成皇后有太姒之德，宜升配睿宗；

translations.literal: Empress Zhaocheng had the virtue of Tai Si and ought to be elevated as consort of Ruizong.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhaocheng had the virtue of Tai Si and ought to be elevated as consort of Ruizong;

sentences.zh: 肅明皇后既非子貴，宜在別廟。

translations.literal: Empress Suming, not having attained eminence through her son, ought to be in a separate temple.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Suming, not having attained eminence through her son, ought to be in a separate temple.

sentences.zh: 周人『奏夷則，歌小呂，以享先妣』。

translations.literal: The Zhou people played the Yi Ze pitch-pipe and sang the Xiao Lü hymn to sacrifice to the ancestral mother.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou people 'played the Yi Ze pitch-pipe and sang the Xiao Lü hymn to sacrifice to the ancestral mother.'

sentences.zh: 先妣，姜原也，以生後稷，故特立廟曰宮。

translations.literal: The ancestral mother was Jiang Yuan, who bore Hou Ji; therefore a separate temple was established called the Gong Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral mother was Jiang Yuan, who bore Hou Ji; therefore a separate temple was established called the Gong Shrine.

sentences.zh: 晉簡文帝鄭宣皇后不配食，築宮於外，以歲時致享。

translations.literal: Empress Xuan of Jin Emperor Jianwen was not given shared offerings; a shrine was built outside, and seasonal sacrifices were offered.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuan of Jin Emperor Jianwen was not given shared offerings; a shrine was built outside, and seasonal sacrifices were offered.

sentences.zh: 肅明請準周姜原、晉宣後，納主別廟，時享如儀。」

translations.literal: For Suming I request following the precedents of Zhou's Jiang Yuan and Jin's Empress Xuan—install the spirit tablet in a separate temple and offer seasonal sacrifices according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: For Suming I request following the precedents of Zhou's Jiang Yuan and Jin's Empress Xuan—install the spirit tablet in a separate temple and offer seasonal sacrifices according to ritual."

sentences.zh: 於是，留主儀坤廟，詔隸太廟，毋置官屬。

translations.literal: Thereupon the spirit tablet was kept in the Yikun Temple, with an edict placing it under the Grand Ancestral Temple and not establishing official staff.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the spirit tablet was kept in the Yikun Temple, with an edict placing it under the Grand Ancestral Temple and not establishing official staff.

sentences.zh: 貞節又與博士蘇獻上言：「睿宗於孝和，弟也。

translations.literal: Zhenjie together with Erudite Su Xian also submitted a memorial: Ruizong was younger brother to Emperor Xiaohé.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenjie together with Erudite Su Xian also submitted a memorial: "Ruizong was younger brother to Emperor Xiaohé.

sentences.zh: 按賀循說，兄弟不相為後。

translations.literal: According to He Xun's explanation, brothers do not succeed one another.
translations.idiomatic: According to He Xun's explanation, brothers do not succeed one another.

sentences.zh: 故殷盤庚不序陽甲，而上繼先君；

translations.literal: Therefore Pan Geng of Yin did not follow Yang Jia in sequence but succeeded upward to the former lord.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Pan Geng of Yin did not follow Yang Jia in sequence but succeeded upward to the former lord;

sentences.zh: 漢光武不嗣孝成，而上承元帝；

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu of Han did not succeed Emperor Xiaocheng but received the line upward from Emperor Yuandi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu of Han did not succeed Emperor Xiaocheng but received the line upward from Emperor Yuandi;

sentences.zh: 晉懷帝繼世祖，不繼惠帝。

translations.literal: Emperor Huai of Jin succeeded Shizu and did not succeed Emperor Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai of Jin succeeded Shizu and did not succeed Emperor Hui.

sentences.zh: 故陽甲、孝成出為別廟。」

translations.literal: Therefore Yang Jia and Emperor Xiaocheng were placed in separate temples.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Yang Jia and Emperor Xiaocheng were placed in separate temples."

sentences.zh: 又言：「兄弟共世，昭穆位同，則毀二廟。

translations.literal: They also said: When brothers share the same generation and their zhao and mu positions are the same, two temples must be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: They also said: "When brothers share the same generation and their zhao and mu positions are the same, two temples must be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 有天下者，從禰而上事七廟，尊者所統廣，故及遠祖。

translations.literal: One who possesses the realm, proceeding upward from the father, serves seven temples; the more exalted one's dominion, the further back one reaches to distant ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: One who possesses the realm, proceeding upward from the father, serves seven temples; the more exalted one's dominion, the further back one reaches to distant ancestors.

sentences.zh: 若容兄弟，則上毀祖考，天子不得全事七世矣。

translations.literal: If brothers are accommodated, then ancestors and forefathers above must be destroyed, and the Son of Heaven cannot fully serve seven generations.
translations.idiomatic: If brothers are accommodated, then ancestors and forefathers above must be destroyed, and the Son of Heaven cannot fully serve seven generations.

sentences.zh: 請以中宗為別廟，大祫則合食太祖。

translations.literal: I request that Emperor Zhongzong be placed in a separate temple, and at the great he sacrifice he be joined in offerings with the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: I request that Emperor Zhongzong be placed in a separate temple, and at the great he sacrifice he be joined in offerings with the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 奉睿宗繼高宗，則祼獻永序。」

translations.literal: Having Ruizong succeed Emperor Gaozong, the libation and offering sequence will be permanently ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Having Ruizong succeed Emperor Gaozong, the libation and offering sequence will be permanently ordered."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved this.

sentences.zh: 乃奉中宗別廟，升睿宗為第七室。

translations.literal: Thereupon Emperor Zhongzong was placed in a separate temple, and Ruizong was elevated to the seventh chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Emperor Zhongzong was placed in a separate temple, and Ruizong was elevated to the seventh chamber.

sentences.zh: 五年，太廟壞，天子舍神主太極殿，營新廟，素服避正寢，三百不朝，猶幸東都。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Grand Ancestral Temple collapsed. The Son of Heaven lodged the spirit tablets in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, built a new temple, wore plain garments and avoided the main palace, did not hold court for three hundred days, yet still visited the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Grand Ancestral Temple collapsed. The Son of Heaven lodged the spirit tablets in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, built a new temple, wore plain garments and avoided the main palace, did not hold court for three hundred days, yet still visited the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 伊闕男子孫平子上書曰：「乃正月太廟毀，此躋二帝之驗也。

translations.literal: Sun Pingzi, a commoner of Yique, submitted a memorial saying: In the first month the Grand Ancestral Temple was destroyed—this is verification of elevating two emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Pingzi, a commoner of Yique, submitted a memorial saying: "In the first month the Grand Ancestral Temple was destroyed—this is verification of elevating two emperors.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》：『君薨，卒哭而祔，祔而作主，特祀於主，烝嘗禘於廟。』

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals: When the lord dies, after the final wailing the tablet is enshrined; after enshrinement the spirit tablet is made; special sacrifices are offered to the tablet; seasonal and di sacrifices are offered in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals: 'When the lord dies, after the final wailing the tablet is enshrined; after enshrinement the spirit tablet is made; special sacrifices are offered to the tablet; seasonal and di sacrifices are offered in the temple.

sentences.zh: 今皆違之。

translations.literal: All of this is now violated.
translations.idiomatic: All of this is now violated.

sentences.zh: 魯文公之二年，躋僖於閔上，後太室壞，《春秋》書其災，說曰：『僖雖閔兄，嘗為之臣，臣居君上，是謂失禮，故太室壞。』

translations.literal: In the second year of Duke Wen of Lu, Duke Xi was elevated above Duke Min; afterward the Grand Chamber collapsed. The Spring and Autumn Annals records this disaster, and the explanation says: Although Xi was Min's elder brother, he had once been his subject; a subject placed above his lord is called a breach of ritual—therefore the Grand Chamber collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Duke Wen of Lu, Duke Xi was elevated above Duke Min; afterward the Grand Chamber collapsed. The Spring and Autumn Annals records this disaster, and the explanation says: 'Although Xi was Min's elder brother, he had once been his subject; a subject placed above his lord is called a breach of ritual—therefore the Grand Chamber collapsed.

sentences.zh: 且兄臣於弟，猶不可躋；

translations.literal: Moreover, when an elder brother had been subject to a younger brother, elevation is still impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when an elder brother had been subject to a younger brother, elevation is still impermissible;

sentences.zh: 弟嘗臣兄，乃可躋乎？

translations.literal: When a younger brother had once been subject to an elder brother—can he be elevated?
translations.idiomatic: when a younger brother had once been subject to an elder brother—can he be elevated?

sentences.zh: 莊公薨，閔公二年而禘，《春秋》非之。

translations.literal: When Duke Zhuang died, in Duke Min's second year a di sacrifice was held—the Spring and Autumn Annals censures this.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Zhuang died, in Duke Min's second year a di sacrifice was held—the Spring and Autumn Annals censures this.

sentences.zh: 況大行夏崩，而太廟冬禘，不亦亟乎？

translations.literal: How much more so when the late emperor died in summer and the Grand Ancestral Temple held a di sacrifice in winter—is this not too hasty?
translations.idiomatic: How much more so when the late emperor died in summer and the Grand Ancestral Temple held a di sacrifice in winter—is this not too hasty?

sentences.zh: 太室尊所，若曰魯自是陵夷，墮周公之祀。

translations.literal: The Grand Chamber is the exalted place; it is as if to say that from this Lu declined and the sacrifices to Duke Zhou were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Chamber is the exalted place; it is as if to say that from this Lu declined and the sacrifices to Duke Zhou were abandoned.

sentences.zh: 太廟今壞，意者其將陵夷，墮先帝之祀乎？

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestral Temple is now destroyed—does this mean it will decline and the sacrifices to former emperors will be abandoned?
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestral Temple is now destroyed—does this mean the dynasty will decline and the sacrifices to former emperors will be abandoned?

sentences.zh: 陛下未祭孝和，先祭太上皇，先臣後君。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has not yet sacrificed to Emperor Xiaohé but first sacrificed to the Grand Emperor—subject before lord.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has not yet sacrificed to Emperor Xiaohé but first sacrificed to the Grand Emperor—subject before lord.

sentences.zh: 昔躋兄弟上，今弟先兄祭。

translations.literal: Formerly brothers were elevated above one another; now the younger brother is sacrificed to before the elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly brothers were elevated above one another; now the younger brother is sacrificed to before the elder brother.

sentences.zh: 昔太室壞，今太廟毀，與《春秋》正同，不可不察。

translations.literal: Formerly the Grand Chamber collapsed; now the Grand Ancestral Temple is destroyed—exactly the same as in the Spring and Autumn Annals. This cannot but be examined.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Grand Chamber collapsed; now the Grand Ancestral Temple is destroyed—exactly the same as in the Spring and Autumn Annals. This must be examined.

sentences.zh: 武後篡國，孝和中興有功，今內主別祠，不得立於世，亦已薄矣。

translations.literal: Empress Wu usurped the realm; Emperor Xiaohé's restoration had merit. Now the inner lord has a separate shrine and cannot stand in the dynastic line—this is already meager enough.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu usurped the realm, yet Emperor Xiaohé's restoration had merit. Now the inner lord has a separate shrine and cannot stand in the dynastic line—this is already meager enough.

sentences.zh: 夫功不可棄，君不可下，長不可輕。

translations.literal: Merit cannot be abandoned; a lord cannot be demoted; an elder cannot be slighted.
translations.idiomatic: Merit cannot be abandoned; a lord cannot be demoted; an elder cannot be slighted.

sentences.zh: 且臣繼君，猶子繼父。

translations.literal: Moreover, a subject succeeding a lord is like a son succeeding a father.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a subject succeeding a lord is like a son succeeding a father.

sentences.zh: 故禹不先鯀，周不先不窋，宋、鄭不以帝乙、厲王不肖，猶尊之也，況中興邪？

translations.literal: Therefore Yu did not place Gun first, Zhou did not place Bu Qiu first; Song and Zheng did not slight Emperor Yi and King Li for their unworthy conduct but still honored them—how much more so for a restoration?
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Yu did not place Gun first, and Zhou did not place Bu Qiu first; Song and Zheng did not slight Emperor Yi and King Li for their unworthy conduct but still honored them—how much more so for a restoration?

sentences.zh: 晉太康時，宣帝廟地陷梁折，又三年，太廟殿陷而及泉，更營之，梁又折。

translations.literal: In the Taikang era of Jin, the ground of Emperor Xuan's temple sank and beams broke; after three more years the Grand Ancestral Temple hall sank to the spring, was rebuilt, and the beams broke again.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taikang era of Jin, the ground of Emperor Xuan's temple sank and beams broke; after three more years the Grand Ancestral Temple hall sank to the spring, was rebuilt, and the beams broke again.

sentences.zh: 天之所譴，非必朽而壞也。

translations.literal: Heaven's reprimand is not necessarily because things are rotten and decayed.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's reprimand is not necessarily because things are rotten and decayed.

sentences.zh: 晉不承天，故及於亂。

translations.literal: Jin did not accept Heaven's mandate, and therefore fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Jin did not accept Heaven's mandate, and therefore fell into disorder.

sentences.zh: 臣謂宜遷孝和還廟，何必違禮，下同魯、晉哉？」

translations.literal: I say Emperor Xiaohé ought to be moved back to the temple—why must we violate ritual and follow the examples of Lu and Jin?
translations.idiomatic: I say Emperor Xiaohé ought to be moved back to the temple—why must we violate ritual and follow the examples of Lu and Jin?

sentences.zh: 帝異其言，詔有司復議。

translations.literal: The emperor was struck by his words and ordered the relevant offices to deliberate again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was struck by his words and ordered the relevant offices to deliberate again.

sentences.zh: 貞節、獻與博士馮宗質之曰：「天子七廟，三昭三穆，與太祖而七。

translations.literal: Zhenjie and Xian together with Erudite Feng Zong debated, saying: The Son of Heaven has seven temples—three zhao and three mu, plus the Grand Ancestor making seven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenjie and Xian together with Erudite Feng Zong debated, saying: "The Son of Heaven has seven temples—three zhao and three mu, plus the Grand Ancestor making seven.

sentences.zh: 父昭子穆，兄弟不與焉。

translations.literal: Father is zhao, son is mu; brothers are not included.
translations.idiomatic: Father is zhao, son is mu; brothers are not included.

sentences.zh: 殷自成湯至帝乙十二君，其父子世六。

translations.literal: From Cheng Tang to Emperor Yi, the twelve lords of Yin had six generations of fathers and sons.
translations.idiomatic: From Cheng Tang to Emperor Yi, the twelve lords of Yin had six generations of fathers and sons.

sentences.zh: 《易乾鑿度》曰：『殷之帝乙六世王。』

translations.literal: The Qian Zao Du of the Book of Changes says: The six generations of kings of Yin's Emperor Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The Qian Zao Du of the Book of Changes says: 'The six generations of kings of Yin's Emperor Yi.

sentences.zh: 則兄弟不為世矣。

translations.literal: Then brothers do not count as generations.
translations.idiomatic: Then brothers do not count as generations.

sentences.zh: 殷人六廟：親廟四，並湯而六。

translations.literal: The six temples of the Yin people: four ancestral temples, plus Tang making six.
translations.idiomatic: The six temples of the Yin people: four ancestral temples, plus Tang making six.

sentences.zh: 殷兄弟四君，若以為世，方上毀四室，乃無祖禰，是必不然。

translations.literal: The four brother-lords of Yin—if considered as generations, one would destroy four chambers above and have no ancestral or immediate-father temples; this surely cannot be so.
translations.idiomatic: The four brother-lords of Yin—if considered as generations, one would destroy four chambers above and have no ancestral or immediate-father temples; this surely cannot be so.

sentences.zh: 古者繇禰極祖，雖叠毀叠遷，而三昭穆未嘗闕也。

translations.literal: In antiquity, proceeding from the immediate father to the highest ancestor, though temples were destroyed and moved in succession, the three zhao and mu were never deficient.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, proceeding from the immediate father to the highest ancestor, though temples were destroyed and moved in succession, the three zhao and mu were never deficient.

sentences.zh: 《禮》：大宗無子，則立支子。

translations.literal: The Rites: When the major lineage has no son, a branch son is established.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites: When the major lineage has no son, a branch son is established.

sentences.zh: 又曰：『為人後者為之子。』

translations.literal: It also says: One who becomes another's successor is counted as that person's son.
translations.idiomatic: It also says: 'One who becomes another's successor is counted as that person's son.

sentences.zh: 無兄弟相為後者，故舍至親，取遠屬。

translations.literal: There is no case of brothers succeeding one another; therefore the closest kin is set aside and a distant member is chosen.
translations.idiomatic: There is no case of brothers succeeding one another; therefore the closest kin is set aside and a distant member is chosen.

sentences.zh: 父子曰繼，兄弟曰及，兄弟不相入廟，尚矣。

translations.literal: Father-to-son is called succession; brother-to-brother is called passing to; brothers do not enter the temple together—this is long established.
translations.idiomatic: Father-to-son is called succession; brother-to-brother is called passing to; brothers do not enter the temple together—this is long established.

sentences.zh: 借有兄弟代立承統，告享不得稱嗣子、嗣孫，乃言伯考、伯祖，何統序乎？

translations.literal: Even supposing brothers alternately established the succession, in announcing sacrifices one could not call them successor son or successor grandson but would speak of deceased elder uncle and deceased elder grandfather—what order of succession would that be?
translations.idiomatic: Even supposing brothers alternately established the succession, in announcing sacrifices one could not call them successor son or successor grandson but would speak of deceased elder uncle and deceased elder grandfather—what order of succession would that be?

sentences.zh: 殷十二君，惟三祖、三宗，明兄弟自為別廟。

translations.literal: Of the twelve lords of Yin, only three ancestors and three honored ones—clearly brothers had separate temples of their own.
translations.idiomatic: Of the twelve lords of Yin, only three ancestors and three honored ones—clearly brothers had separate temples of their own.

sentences.zh: 漢世祖列七廟，而惠帝不與。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu of Han listed seven temples, and Emperor Hui was not included.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu of Han listed seven temples, and Emperor Hui was not included.

sentences.zh: 文、武子孫昌衍，文為漢太宗。

translations.literal: The descendants of King Wen and King Wu flourished; King Wen was Han's Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The descendants of King Wen and King Wu flourished; King Wen was Han's Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 晉景帝亦文帝兄，景絕世，不列於廟。

translations.literal: Jingdi of Jin was also Emperor Wen's elder brother; with Jing's line extinct, he was not placed in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Jingdi of Jin was also Emperor Wen's elder brother; with Jing's line extinct, he was not placed in the temple.

sentences.zh: 及告謚世祖，稱景為從祖。

translations.literal: When announcing Shizu's posthumous title they called Jing a distant grandfather.
translations.idiomatic: When announcing Shizu's posthumous title they called Jing a distant grandfather.

sentences.zh: 今謂晉武帝越崇其父，而廟毀及亡，何漢出惠帝而享世長久乎？

translations.literal: Now you say Jin Emperor Wu excessively exalted his father and the temple was destroyed leading to ruin—why did Han exclude Emperor Hui yet enjoy long-lasting fortune?
translations.idiomatic: Now you say Jin Emperor Wu excessively exalted his father and the temple was destroyed leading to ruin—why did Han exclude Emperor Hui yet enjoy long-lasting fortune?

sentences.zh: 七廟、五廟，明天子、諸侯也；
