translations.literal: Seven temples and five temples distinguish the Son of Heaven and feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Seven temples and five temples distinguish the Son of Heaven and feudal lords;

sentences.zh: 父子相繼，一統也；

translations.literal: Father and son succeeding one another is a single succession.
translations.idiomatic: father and son succeeding one another is a single succession;

sentences.zh: 昭穆列序，重繼也。

translations.literal: The zhao-mu ordering is the weight of succession.
translations.idiomatic: the zhao-mu ordering is the weight of succession.

sentences.zh: 禮，兄弟相繼，不得稱嗣子，明睿宗不父孝和，必上繼高宗者。

translations.literal: Ritual: when brothers succeed one another they may not be called successor son—clearly Ruizong did not take Xiaohé as father but must succeed upward to Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual: when brothers succeed one another they may not be called successor son—clearly Ruizong did not take Xiaohé as father but must succeed upward to Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 偶室於廟，則為二穆，於禮可乎？

translations.literal: Adjacent chambers in the temple would make two mu—is this permissible by ritual?
translations.idiomatic: Adjacent chambers in the temple would make two mu—is this permissible by ritual?

sentences.zh: 禮所不可，而使天子旁紹伯考，棄己親正統哉？

translations.literal: What ritual forbids, yet would have the Son of Heaven adopt a deceased elder uncle by collateral succession and abandon his own proper legitimate line?
translations.idiomatic: What ritual forbids, yet would have the Son of Heaven adopt a deceased elder uncle by collateral succession and abandon his own proper legitimate line?

sentences.zh: 孝和中興，別建園寢，百世不毀，尚何議哉？

translations.literal: Xiaohé's restoration separately established a garden tomb that would not be destroyed for a hundred generations—what further debate is needed?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaohé's restoration separately established a garden tomb that would not be destroyed for a hundred generations—what further debate is needed?

sentences.zh: 平子猥引僖公逆祀為比，殊不知孝和升新寢，聖真方祔廟，則未嘗一日居上也。」

translations.literal: Pingzi rashly cited Duke Xi's improper sacrifice as a parallel, not knowing that Xiaohé was elevated to a new tomb while Sheng Zhen was just being enshrined in the temple—they never occupied a higher position for even a day.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzi rashly cited Duke Xi's improper sacrifice as a parallel, not knowing that Xiaohé was elevated to a new tomb while Sheng Zhen was just being enshrined in the temple—they never occupied a higher position for even a day."

sentences.zh: 帝語宰相召平子與博士詳論。

translations.literal: The emperor told the chief ministers to summon Pingzi and the erudites for detailed debate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the chief ministers to summon Pingzi and the erudites for detailed debate.

sentences.zh: 博士護前言，合軋平子。

translations.literal: The erudites defended their earlier statements and combined to suppress Pingzi.
translations.idiomatic: The erudites defended their earlier statements and combined to suppress Pingzi.

sentences.zh: 平子援經辯數分明，獻等不能屈。

translations.literal: Pingzi cited the classics with clear numbered arguments; Xian and the others could not refute him.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzi cited the classics with clear numbered arguments; Xian and the others could not refute him.

sentences.zh: 蘇颋右博士，故平子坐貶都城尉。

translations.literal: Su Ting sided with the erudites, and therefore Pingzi was demoted to Commandant of the Capital District.
translations.idiomatic: Su Ting sided with the erudites, and therefore Pingzi was demoted to Commandant of the Capital District.

sentences.zh: 然諸儒以平子孤挺，見迮於禮官，不平。

translations.literal: Yet the Confucians, because Pingzi stood alone, saw him oppressed by the ritual officials and were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Confucians, because Pingzi stood alone, saw him oppressed by the ritual officials and were displeased.

sentences.zh: 帝亦知其直，久不決，然卒不復中宗於廟。

translations.literal: The emperor also knew he was upright; long unable to decide, yet in the end did not restore Zhongzong to the temple.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also knew he was upright; long unable to decide, yet in the end did not restore Zhongzong to the temple.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝將大享明堂，貞節惡武後所營，非古所謂「木不鏤、土不文」之制，乃與馮宗上言：「明堂必直丙巳，以憲房、心布政，太微上帝之所。

Zhenjie disliked what Empress Wu had built, which was not the ancient system of 'wood unadorned, earth unembellished,' and together with Feng Zong submitted a memorial: The Bright Hall must face bing and si, to receive governance from the Fang and Xin asterisms; the Supreme Palace is where the Supreme God resides.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor was about to perform the great sacrifice at the Bright Hall. sentences.zh: 武後始以乾元正寢占陽午地，先帝所以聽政，故毀殿作堂。

translations.literal: Empress Wu initially took the Qianyuan main palace occupying the yang-wu position; the former emperor held court there, so the hall was demolished to make the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu initially took the Qianyuan main palace occupying the yang-wu position; the former emperor held court there, so the hall was demolished to make the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 撤之日，有音如雷，庶民嘩訕，以為神靈不悅。

translations.literal: On the day of demolition there was a sound like thunder; the common people clamored and mocked, believing the spirits were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of demolition there was a sound like thunder; the common people clamored and mocked, believing the spirits were displeased.

sentences.zh: 堂成，災火從之。

translations.literal: When the hall was completed, disaster fire followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the hall was completed, disaster fire followed.

sentences.zh: 後不脩德，俄復營構，殫用極侈，詭禳厥變，又欲嚴配上帝，神安肯臨？

translations.literal: Later she did not cultivate virtue and soon built again, exhausting resources in extreme extravagance, performing strange rites to avert the calamity, yet also wishing to join the Supreme God in sacrifice—would the spirits consent to descend?
translations.idiomatic: Later she did not cultivate virtue and soon built again, exhausting resources in extreme extravagance, performing strange rites to avert the calamity, yet also wishing to join the Supreme God in sacrifice—would the spirits consent to descend?

sentences.zh: 且密邇掖廷，人神雜擾，是謂不可放物者也。

translations.literal: Moreover it is close to the inner palace, with human and divine affairs mixed in disorder—this is what is called a place where things cannot be left loose.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover it is close to the inner palace, with human and divine affairs mixed in disorder—this is what is called a place where things cannot be left loose.

sentences.zh: 二京上都，四方是則。

translations.literal: The two capitals and the upper capital are the model for all directions.
translations.idiomatic: The two capitals and the upper capital are the model for all directions.

sentences.zh: 天子聽政，乃居便坐，無以尊示群臣。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven holds court from a convenient seat, with no way to display majesty to the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven holds court from a convenient seat, with no way to display majesty to the ministers.

sentences.zh: 願以明堂復為乾元殿，使人識其舊，不亦愈乎？」

translations.literal: I wish that the Bright Hall be restored to the Qianyuan Hall, so people may recognize its former state—is this not better?
translations.idiomatic: I wish that the Bright Hall be restored to the Qianyuan Hall, so people may recognize its former state—is this not better?"

sentences.zh: 詔所司詳議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the relevant offices to deliberate in detail.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書王誌愔等僉謂：「明堂瑰怪不法，天燼之餘，不容大享。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Wang Zhikan and others unanimously said: The Bright Hall is bizarre and unlawful; after heaven's burning, it cannot accommodate the great sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Wang Zhikan and others unanimously said: "The Bright Hall is bizarre and unlawful; after heaven's burning, it cannot accommodate the great sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 請因舊循制，還署乾元正寢。

translations.literal: I request following the old system and restoring the Qianyuan main palace.
translations.idiomatic: I request following the old system and restoring the Qianyuan main palace.

sentences.zh: 正、至，天子禦以朝會。

translations.literal: At the winter and summer solstices the Son of Heaven would hold court there for assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter and summer solstices the Son of Heaven would hold court there for assemblies.

sentences.zh: 若大享，復寓圜丘。」

translations.literal: For the great sacrifice, the Round Mound would again serve as the temporary site.
translations.idiomatic: For the great sacrifice, the Round Mound would again serve as the temporary site."

sentences.zh: 制曰可。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved this.

sentences.zh: 貞節以壽卒。

translations.literal: Zhenjie died of old age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenjie died of old age.

sentences.zh: 施敬本

translations.literal: Shi Jingben
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingben

sentences.zh: 施敬本，潤州丹陽人。

translations.literal: Shi Jingben was a native of Danyang in Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingben was a native of Danyang in Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 開元中，為四門助教。

translations.literal: During Kaiyuan he served as Simen Assistant Instructor.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan he served as Simen Assistant Instructor.

sentences.zh: 玄宗將封禪，詔有司講求典儀。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong was about to perform the feng and shan sacrifices and ordered the relevant offices to study and seek canonical ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong was about to perform the feng and shan sacrifices and ordered the relevant offices to study and seek canonical ritual.

sentences.zh: 舊制，盥手、洗爵，皆侍中主之；

translations.literal: Under the old system, washing hands and washing the goblet were both presided over by the Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, washing hands and washing the goblet were both presided over by the Palace Attendant;

sentences.zh: 詔祀天神，太祝主之。

translations.literal: The edict for sacrificing to the Heavenly Spirit was presided over by the Grand Invocator.
translations.idiomatic: the edict for sacrificing to the Heavenly Spirit was presided over by the Grand Invocator.

sentences.zh: 敬本上言曰：「周制，大宗伯郁人，下士二，掌祼事。

translations.literal: Jingben submitted a memorial saying: Under Zhou institutions, the Chief Ritual Master had two libation officers of lower servitor rank who managed libation affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jingben submitted a memorial saying: "Under Zhou institutions, the Chief Ritual Master had two libation officers of lower servitor rank who managed libation affairs.

sentences.zh: 漢無郁人，用近臣。

translations.literal: Han had no libation officer and used close ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Han had no libation officer and used close ministers.

sentences.zh: 漢世侍中微甚，籍孺、閎孺等幸臣為之。

translations.literal: In Han times the Palace Attendant was a very minor post; favored ministers such as Ji Ru and Hong Ru held it.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times the Palace Attendant was a very minor post; favored ministers such as Ji Ru and Hong Ru held it.

sentences.zh: 後漢邵闔自侍中遷步兵校尉，秩千石，其職省起居，執虎子，蓋褻臣也。

translations.literal: Later in Han, Shao He moved from Palace Attendant to Commandant of the Footsoldiers, rank one thousand shi; his duties included recording the emperor's movements and holding the tiger vessel—he was essentially an intimate attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Later in Han, Shao He moved from Palace Attendant to Commandant of the Footsoldiers, rank one thousand shi; his duties included recording the emperor's movements and holding the tiger vessel—he was essentially an intimate attendant.

sentences.zh: 今侍中位宰相，非郁人比。

translations.literal: Today the Palace Attendant ranks with the chief minister and is not comparable to a libation officer.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Palace Attendant ranks with the chief minister and is not comparable to a libation officer.

sentences.zh: 祝者薦主人意於神，非賤職也。

translations.literal: The invocator conveys the host's intent to the spirits—it is not a lowly office.
translations.idiomatic: The invocator conveys the host's intent to the spirits—it is not a lowly office.

sentences.zh: 古二君相見，卿為上儐，況天人際哉！

translations.literal: In antiquity when two lords met, a minister served as chief usher—how much more so at the boundary between Heaven and man!
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity when two lords met, a minister served as chief usher—how much more so at the boundary between Heaven and man!

sentences.zh: 周太祝，下大夫二，上士四。

translations.literal: Zhou's Grand Invocator had two lower grand masters and four upper servitors.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's Grand Invocator had two lower grandees and four upper servitors.

sentences.zh: 下大夫，今郎中、太常丞之比；

translations.literal: Lower grand master corresponds to today's Gentleman of the Palace and Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Lower grand master corresponds to today's Gentleman of the Palace and Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 上士，員外郎、博士之比。

translations.literal: Upper servitor corresponds to outside-office gentleman and erudite.
translations.idiomatic: upper servitor corresponds to outside-office gentleman and erudite.

sentences.zh: 漢太祝令秩六百石，今太祝乃下士。

translations.literal: Han's Director of Invocations had rank six hundred shi; today's Grand Invocator is only a lower servitor.
translations.idiomatic: Han's Director of Invocations had rank six hundred shi; today's Grand Invocator is only a lower servitor.

sentences.zh: 以下士接天，以大臣奉天子，輕重不倫，非禮也。

translations.literal: To use a lower servitor to receive Heaven and a great minister to serve the Son of Heaven—the weight is disproportionate and not ritual.
translations.idiomatic: To use a lower servitor to receive Heaven and a great minister to serve the Son of Heaven—the weight is disproportionate and not ritual.

sentences.zh: 舊制，謁者引太尉升壇。

translations.literal: Under the old system, the usher led the Grand Commandant up the altar.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, the usher led the Grand Commandant up the altar.

sentences.zh: 謁者位下，升壇禮重。

translations.literal: The usher's rank was low, yet the altar ascent ritual was weighty.
translations.idiomatic: The usher's rank was low, yet the altar ascent ritual was weighty.

sentences.zh: 漢尚書御史屬，有謁者僕射一，秩六百石，銅印青綬；

translations.literal: Han's Masters of Writing and Censorate had one Usher Superintendent, rank six hundred shi, with bronze seal and blue sash.
translations.idiomatic: Han's Masters of Writing and Censorate had one Usher Superintendent, rank six hundred shi, with bronze seal and blue sash;

sentences.zh: 謁者三十五，以郎中滿歲稱給事中，未滿歲稱謁者。

translations.literal: Thirty-five ushers—when a Gentleman of the Palace completed a year he was called Attendant Within the Gates; before completing a year he was called Usher.
translations.idiomatic: thirty-five ushers—when a Gentleman of the Palace completed a year he was called Attendant Within the Gates; before completing a year he was called Usher.

sentences.zh: 光祿勛屬，有謁者，掌賓贊，員七十，秩比六百石。

translations.literal: Under the Director of Bright Harmony were ushers managing guest reception, seventy in number, rank equivalent to six hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Director of Bright Harmony were ushers managing guest reception, seventy in number, rank equivalent to six hundred shi.

sentences.zh: 則古謁者名秩差異等，今謁者班微，循空名，忘實事，非所以事天也。」

translations.literal: Thus ancient ushers differed in name and rank; today's ushers are of low rank, clinging to empty titles and forgetting substantive duties—this is not how to serve Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ancient ushers differed in name and rank; today's ushers are of low rank, clinging to empty titles and forgetting substantive duties—this is not how to serve Heaven."

sentences.zh: 帝詔中書令張說引敬本熟悉其議，故侍中、祝、謁者，視禮輕重，以它官攝領。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Chief Secretariat Director Zhang Yue to summon Jingben, who was well versed in these deliberations; therefore for Palace Attendant, Invocator, and Usher, according to the weight of ritual, other officials were appointed to act in their stead.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Chief Secretariat Director Zhang Yue to summon Jingben, who was well versed in these deliberations; therefore for Palace Attendant, Invocator, and Usher, according to the weight of ritual, other officials were appointed to act in their stead.

sentences.zh: 敬本以太常博士為集賢院脩撰。

translations.literal: Jingben served as Compiler at the Hall of Assembled Worthies from his post as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Jingben served as Compiler at the Hall of Assembled Worthies from his post as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 逾年，遷右補闕、秘書郎，卒。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Right Supplementation Censor and Secretary; he died.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was transferred to Right Supplementation Censor and Secretary; he died.

sentences.zh: 盧履冰

translations.literal: Lu Lübing
translations.idiomatic: Lu Lübing

sentences.zh: 盧履冰，幽州范陽人，元魏都官尚書義僖五世孫。

translations.literal: Lu Lübing was a native of Fanyang in Youzhou, fifth-generation descendant of Yixi, Director of the Central Office of Northern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Lübing was a native of Fanyang in Youzhou, fifth-generation descendant of Yixi, Director of the Central Office of Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 開元五年，仕歷右補闕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan he served successively as Right Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan he served successively as Right Supplementation Censor.

sentences.zh: 建言：「古者父在為母期，徹靈而心喪。

translations.literal: He submitted a proposal: In antiquity when the father was alive mourning for the mother was one year, with the spirit tablet removed and inner mourning observed.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a proposal: "In antiquity when the father was alive mourning for the mother was one year, with the spirit tablet removed and inner mourning observed.

sentences.zh: 武後始請同父三年，非是，請如禮便。」

translations.literal: Empress Wu first requested three years equal to the father—this was wrong; I request following ritual as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu first requested three years equal to the father—this was wrong; I request following ritual as convenient."

sentences.zh: 玄宗疑之，又以舅、嫂叔服未安，並下百官議。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong was uncertain, and because mourning for maternal uncles, sisters-in-law, and paternal uncles was also unsettled, he submitted the matter to all officials for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong was uncertain, and because mourning for maternal uncles, sisters-in-law, and paternal uncles was also unsettled, he submitted the matter to all officials for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 刑部郎中田再思曰：「會禮之家比聚訟。

translations.literal: Director of the Penal Bureau Tian Zaosi said: Families gathered to discuss ritual are like gathering lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Penal Bureau Tian Zaosi said: "Families gathered to discuss ritual are like gathering lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 循古不必是，而行今未必非。

translations.literal: Following antiquity is not necessarily correct, and following the present is not necessarily wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Following antiquity is not necessarily correct, and following the present is not necessarily wrong.

sentences.zh: 父在為母三年，高宗實行之，著令已久。

translations.literal: Three years mourning for the mother while the father lives—Emperor Gaozong actually implemented this and it has been recorded in statutes for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Three years mourning for the mother while the father lives—Emperor Gaozong actually implemented this and it has been recorded in statutes for a long time.

sentences.zh: 何必乖先帝之旨，閡人子之情，愛一期服於其親，使與伯叔母、姑姊妹同？

translations.literal: Why must we go against the former emperor's intent, obstruct a son's feelings, and restrict one period of mourning for one's parent to make it the same as for paternal aunts, paternal uncles' wives, and paternal aunts and sisters?
translations.idiomatic: Why must we go against the former emperor's intent, obstruct a son's feelings, and restrict one period of mourning for one's parent to make it the same as for paternal aunts, paternal uncles' wives, and paternal aunts and sisters?

sentences.zh: 嫂叔、舅甥服，太宗實制之，閱百年無異論，不可改。」

translations.literal: Mourning for sister-in-law, paternal uncle, and maternal uncle and nephew—Emperor Taizong actually established this; for a hundred years there has been no dissent—it cannot be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning for sister-in-law, paternal uncle, and maternal uncle and nephew—Emperor Taizong actually established this; for a hundred years there has been no dissent—it cannot be changed."

sentences.zh: 履冰因言：「上元中，父在為母三年，後雖請，未用也，逮垂拱始行之。

translations.literal: Lübing then said: In the Shangyuan era, three years mourning for the mother while the father lives—though later requested, it was not used; only in the Chuigong era was it implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Lübing then said: "In the Shangyuan era, three years mourning for the mother while the father lives—though later requested, it was not used; only in the Chuigong era was it implemented.

sentences.zh: 至有祖父母在而子孫婦沒，行服再期，不可謂宜。

translations.literal: There were cases where grandparents were alive yet daughters-in-law died and mourning was observed for two periods—this cannot be called proper.
translations.idiomatic: There were cases where grandparents were alive yet daughters-in-law died and mourning was observed for two periods—this cannot be called proper.

sentences.zh: 禮，女子無專道，故曰『家無二尊』。

translations.literal: Ritual: a woman has no independent way, therefore it says 'a household has no two exalted ones.'
translations.idiomatic: Ritual: a woman has no independent way, therefore it says 'a household has no two exalted ones.'

sentences.zh: 父在為母服期，統一尊也。

translations.literal: One year mourning for the mother while the father lives unifies a single exalted authority.
translations.idiomatic: One year mourning for the mother while the father lives unifies a single exalted authority.

sentences.zh: 今不正其失，恐後世復有婦奪夫之敗，不可不察。」

translations.literal: If this error is not corrected now, I fear later ages will again have the disaster of wives usurping husbands—it cannot but be examined.
translations.idiomatic: If this error is not corrected now, I fear later ages will again have the disaster of wives usurping husbands—it must be examined."

sentences.zh: 書留未下。

translations.literal: The memorial was kept and not issued.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was kept and not issued.

sentences.zh: 履冰即極陳：「父在為母立几筵者一期，心喪者再期，父必三年而後娶，以達子之誌。

translations.literal: Lübing then argued at length: When the father is alive mourning for the mother sets up the offering table for one period; inner mourning lasts two periods; the father must wait three years before remarrying, to fulfill the son's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Lübing then argued at length: "When the father is alive mourning for the mother sets up the offering table for one period; inner mourning lasts two periods; the father must wait three years before remarrying, to fulfill the son's intent.

sentences.zh: 夫聖人豈蔑情於所生？

translations.literal: Would the sages scorn feeling for those who bore them?
translations.idiomatic: Would the sages scorn feeling for those who bore them?

sentences.zh: 固有意於天下。

translations.literal: They surely had intent for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: They surely had intent for all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 昔武後陰儲篡謀，豫自光崇，升期[B18J]，抗斬衰，俄而乘陵唐家，以啟釁階。

translations.literal: In the past Empress Wu secretly stored usurpation in her heart, elevating herself in advance to one-year qi mourning and donning cut-sackcloth mourning, and soon overbore the Tang house, opening the path to calamity.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Empress Wu secretly stored usurpation in her heart, elevating herself in advance to one-year qi mourning and donning cut-sackcloth mourning, and soon overbore the Tang house, opening the path to calamity.

sentences.zh: 孝和僅得反正，韋氏復出，冘殺天子，幾亡宗社。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaohé barely managed restoration; Empress Wei rose again, wantonly killed the Son of Heaven, and nearly destroyed the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaohé barely managed restoration; Empress Wei rose again, wantonly killed the Son of Heaven, and nearly destroyed the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 故臣將以正夫婦之綱，非特母子間也。

translations.literal: Therefore I wish to rectify the bond of husband and wife—not only the relation between mother and son.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I wish to rectify the bond of husband and wife—not only the relation between mother and son.

sentences.zh: 議者或言：『降母服，非《詩》所謂罔極者，而又與伯叔母、姑姊妹等。

translations.literal: Some debaters say: Reducing mourning for the mother is not what the Odes calls boundless feeling, and moreover makes it the same as for paternal aunts, paternal uncles' wives, and paternal aunts and sisters.
translations.idiomatic: Some debaters say: 'Reducing mourning for the mother is not what the Odes calls boundless feeling, and moreover makes it the same as for paternal aunts, paternal uncles' wives, and paternal aunts and sisters.

sentences.zh: 且[B18J]、斬已有升降，則歲月不容異也。』

translations.literal: Moreover qi and zhan already have gradations in rank, so the months cannot be made different.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover qi and zhan already have gradations in rank, so the months cannot be made different.

sentences.zh: 此迂生鄙儒，未習先王之旨，安足議夫禮哉？

translations.literal: These are narrow pedants who have not studied the intent of the former kings—how can they discuss ritual?
translations.idiomatic: These are narrow pedants who have not studied the intent of the former kings—how can they discuss ritual?

sentences.zh: 罔極者，春秋祭祀，以時思之，謂君子有終身之憂之謂，何限一期、二期服哉？

translations.literal: Boundless feeling means spring and autumn sacrifices and timely remembrance—what the gentleman calls lifelong sorrow; how can it be limited to one or two periods of mourning?
translations.idiomatic: Boundless feeling means spring and autumn sacrifices and timely remembrance—what the gentleman calls lifelong sorrow; how can it be limited to one or two periods of mourning?

sentences.zh: 聖人之於禮，必建中制，使賢不肖共成文理而後釋，彼伯叔、姑姊，烏有筵杖之制、三年心喪乎？

translations.literal: The sages in ritual must establish a middle standard, so that worthy and unworthy alike complete the pattern of ritual before release; do paternal aunts and sisters have regulations for offering tables and mourning staffs or three years of inner mourning?
translations.idiomatic: The sages in ritual must establish a middle standard, so that worthy and unworthy alike complete the pattern of ritual before release; do paternal aunts and sisters have regulations for offering tables and mourning staffs or three years of inner mourning?

sentences.zh: 左散騎常侍元行沖議曰：「古緣情制服：女天父，妻天夫，斬衰三年，情禮俱盡者，因心立極也。

translations.literal: Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Horse Yuan Xingchong debated: In antiquity ritual garments followed feeling: the daughter looks to Heaven through the father, the wife through the husband; cut-sackcloth for three years where feeling and ritual are both exhausted—this establishes the utmost from the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Horse Yuan Xingchong debated: "In antiquity ritual garments followed feeling: the daughter looks to Heaven through the father, the wife through the husband; cut-sackcloth for three years where feeling and ritual are both exhausted—this establishes the utmost from the heart.

sentences.zh: 妻喪杖期，情禮俱殺者，遠嫌疑，尊乾道也。

translations.literal: Mourning for the wife with staff for one period, where feeling and ritual are both reduced, keeps distant suspicion and honors the yang Way.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning for the wife with staff for one period, where feeling and ritual are both reduced, keeps distant suspicion and honors the yang Way.

sentences.zh: 為嫡子三年斬衰而不去官，尊祖重嫡，崇其禮，殺其情也。

translations.literal: For the legitimate son three years cut-sackcloth without leaving office honors the ancestor, exalts the legitimate heir, elevates the ritual and reduces the feeling.
translations.idiomatic: For the legitimate son three years cut-sackcloth without leaving office honors the ancestor, exalts the legitimate heir, elevates the ritual and reduces the feeling.

sentences.zh: 孝莫大於嚴父，故父在為母免官，[B18J]而期，心喪三年，情已申而禮殺也，自堯、舜、周公、孔子所同。

translations.literal: Nothing exceeds honoring the father in filial piety; therefore when the father is alive mourning for the mother requires leaving office, qi for one period, inner mourning three years—feeling is expressed but ritual is reduced—the same from Yao, Shun, Duke Zhou, and Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing exceeds honoring the father in filial piety; therefore when the father is alive mourning for the mother requires leaving office, qi for one period, inner mourning three years—feeling is expressed but ritual is reduced—the same from Yao, Shun, Duke Zhou, and Confucius.

sentences.zh: 而今舍尊厭之重，虧嚴父之義，謂之禮，可乎？

translations.literal: Now abandoning the weight of honoring what is exalted, impairing the righteousness of honoring the father, and calling it ritual—can this be?
translations.idiomatic: Now abandoning the weight of honoring what is exalted, impairing the righteousness of honoring the father, and calling it ritual—can this be?

sentences.zh: 姨兼從母之名，以母之女黨，加於舅服，不為無理。

translations.literal: Aunt combines the name of following mother; as the mother's female kin, adding mourning for the maternal uncle is not without reason.
translations.idiomatic: Aunt combines the name of following mother; as the mother's female kin, adding mourning for the maternal uncle is not without reason.

sentences.zh: 嫂叔不服，則遠嫌也。

translations.literal: Sister-in-law and paternal uncle do not wear mourning for each other—this keeps distant suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Sister-in-law and paternal uncle do not wear mourning for each other—this keeps distant suspicion.

translations.literal: The emperor did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not reply.

sentences.zh: 是時言喪服，各以所見奮，交口紛騰。

translations.literal: At that time those who spoke on mourning garments each argued from their own view, mouths crossing in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: At that time those who spoke on mourning garments each argued from their own view, mouths crossing in uproar.

sentences.zh: 七年，乃下詔：「服紀一用古制。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year an edict was finally issued: Mourning regulations shall uniformly follow the ancient system.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year an edict was finally issued: "Mourning regulations shall uniformly follow the ancient system."

sentences.zh: 自是人間父在為母服，或期而禫，禫而釋，心喪三年；

translations.literal: Thereafter among the people mourning for the mother while the father lived was either one period then end of mourning garments, end of garments then release, with inner mourning three years.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter among the people mourning for the mother while the father lived was either one period then end of mourning garments, end of garments then release, with inner mourning three years;

sentences.zh: 或期而禫，終三年；

translations.literal: or one period then end of garments, continuing three years.
translations.idiomatic: or one period then end of garments, continuing three years;

translations.literal: or three years qi mourning.
translations.idiomatic: or three years qi mourning.

sentences.zh: 後履冰以官卒。

translations.literal: Later Lübing died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lübing died in office.

sentences.zh: 王仲丘

translations.literal: Wang Zhongqiu
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongqiu

sentences.zh: 王仲丘，沂州瑯邪人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongqiu was a native of Langya in Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongqiu was a native of Langya in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 祖師順，仕高宗，議漕輸事有名當時，終司門郎中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shi Shun served Emperor Gaozong, was famous in his day for deliberating transport by canal, and ended as Director of the Gate Office.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shi Shun served Emperor Gaozong, was famous in his day for deliberating transport by canal, and ended as Director of the Gate Office.

sentences.zh: 仲丘開元中歷左補闕內供奉、集賢脩撰、起居舍人。

translations.literal: Zhongqiu during Kaiyuan served successively as Left Supplementation Censor with inner palace appointment, Compiler at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and Diarist of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqiu during Kaiyuan served successively as Left Supplementation Censor with inner palace appointment, Compiler at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and Diarist of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時典章差駁，仲丘欲合《貞觀》、《顯慶》二禮，據「有其舉之，莫可廢之」之誼，即上言：「《貞觀禮》，正月上辛，祀感帝於南郊。

translations.literal: At that time canonical regulations were inconsistent; Zhongqiu wished to combine the Zhenguan and Xianqing rituals, relying on the principle that what has been instituted must not be abolished, and submitted a memorial: The Zhenguan Rites on the first month upper xin day sacrifice to the Lord of Felt at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: At that time canonical regulations were inconsistent; Zhongqiu wished to combine the Zhenguan and Xianqing rituals, relying on the principle that what has been instituted must not be abolished, and submitted a memorial: "The Zhenguan Rites on the first month upper xin day sacrifice to the Lord of Felt at the southern suburb.

translations.literal: The Xianqing Rites: sacrifice to the August Heaven God at the Round Mound to pray for grain.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianqing Rites: sacrifice to the August Heaven God at the Round Mound to pray for grain.

sentences.zh: 臣謂《詩》『春夏祈谷於上帝』，《禮》『上辛祈谷於上帝』，則上帝當昊天矣。

translations.literal: I say the Odes 'in spring and summer pray for grain to the Lord on High,' and the Rites 'on upper xin pray for grain to the Lord on High'—then the Lord on High is the August Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I say the Odes 'in spring and summer pray for grain to the Lord on High,' and the Rites 'on upper xin pray for grain to the Lord on High'—then the Lord on High is the August Heaven.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄曰：『天之五帝遞王，王者必感一以興。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says: The Five Thearchs of Heaven succeed one another in kingship; the king must be moved by one to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan says: 'The Five Thearchs of Heaven succeed one another in kingship; the king must be moved by one to rise.

translations.idiomatic: Compare to sacrificing in the first month of summer at the suburb to the one from whom one was born, with one's ancestor as consort, and thereby praying for grain.

translations.literal: Sacrifice to the Lord of Felt—the Zhenguan Rites used it.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice to the Lord of Felt—the Zhenguan Rites used it.

sentences.zh: 請因祈谷之壇，遍祭五方帝。

translations.literal: I request at the altar for praying for grain to sacrifice broadly to the Five Directional Thearchs.
translations.idiomatic: I request at the altar for praying for grain to sacrifice broadly to the Five Directional Thearchs.

sentences.zh: 五帝者，五行之精，九谷之宗也。

translations.literal: The Five Thearchs are the essences of the Five Phases, the lords of the nine grains.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Thearchs are the essences of the Five Phases, the lords of the nine grains.

translations.idiomatic: I request both rituals be used.

translations.literal: The Zhenguan Rites: at the rain sacrifice sacrifice to the Five Directional Thearchs, Five Human Thearchs, and Five Officials at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenguan Rites: at the rain sacrifice, sacrifice to the Five Directional Thearchs, Five Human Thearchs, and Five Officials at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 《顯慶禮》，祀昊天上帝於圓丘。

translations.literal: The Xianqing Rites: sacrifice to the August Heaven God at the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianqing Rites: sacrifice to the August Heaven God at the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 臣謂雩上帝，為百谷祈甘雨，故《月令》：『大雩帝，用盛樂。』

translations.literal: I say praying to the Lord on High for the hundred grains seeks sweet rain; therefore the Monthly Ordinances: 'Great rain sacrifice to the Lord, using grand music.'
translations.idiomatic: I say praying to the Lord on High for the hundred grains seeks sweet rain; therefore the Monthly Ordinances: 'Great rain sacrifice to the Lord, using grand music.'

sentences.zh: 鄭玄說：『帝，上帝也，乃天別號。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan explains: Lord means the Lord on High—it is Heaven's separate title.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan explains: 'Lord means the Lord on High—it is Heaven's separate title.

translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice at the Round Mound honors Heaven's position.

translations.literal: The Xianqing sacrifice to the August Heaven matches the Monthly Ordinances, yet the Zhenguan Rites once sacrificed to the Five Thearchs—I request both rituals be used.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianqing sacrifice to the August Heaven matches the Monthly Ordinances, yet the Zhenguan Rites once sacrificed to the Five Thearchs—I request both rituals be used.

translations.idiomatic: The Zhenguan Rites: in late autumn sacrifice to the Five Directional Thearchs and Five Officials at the Bright Hall.

translations.idiomatic: The Xianqing Rites: sacrifice to the August Heaven God at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 臣謂周郊祀後稷以配天，宗祀文王於明堂以配上帝。

translations.literal: I say Zhou at the suburban sacrifice paired Hou Ji with Heaven; at the ancestral sacrifice honored King Wen in the Bright Hall paired with the Lord on High.
translations.idiomatic: I say Zhou at the suburban sacrifice paired Hou Ji with Heaven; at the ancestral sacrifice honored King Wen in the Bright Hall paired with the Lord on High.

sentences.zh: 先儒以天為感帝，引太微五帝著之上帝，則屬之昊天。

translations.literal: Early Confucians took Heaven as the Lord of Felt, citing the Five Thearchs of the Supreme Palace as belonging to the Lord on High—then they belong to the August Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Early Confucians took Heaven as the Lord of Felt, citing the Five Thearchs of the Supreme Palace as belonging to the Lord on High—then they belong to the August Heaven.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄稱《周官》旅上帝，祀五帝，各文而異禮，不容並而為一。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan said the Offices of Zhou 'procession to the Lord on High' sacrifices to the Five Thearchs, each with different pattern and different ritual—they cannot be combined into one.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan said the Offices of Zhou 'procession to the Lord on High' sacrifices to the Five Thearchs, each with different pattern and different ritual—they cannot be combined into one.

sentences.zh: 故於《孝經》天、上帝，申之曰：『上帝亦天也。』

translations.idiomatic: Therefore in the Classic of Filial Piety regarding Heaven and the Lord on High he explained: 'The Lord on High is also Heaven.'

translations.literal: Spirits have no two lords—only the place differs, to avoid Hou Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits have no two lords—only the place differs, to avoid Hou Ji.

sentences.zh: 今《顯慶》享上帝，合於《經》，然《貞觀》嘗祀五方帝矣。

translations.literal: Now the Xianqing offering to the Lord on High matches the Classic, yet the Zhenguan Rites once sacrificed to the Five Directional Thearchs.

translations.idiomatic: An edict approved this.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Assistant Master of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Assistant Master of Rites.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈秘書少監。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.

translations.literal: Kang Ziyuan
translations.idiomatic: Kang Ziyuan

sentences.zh: 康子元，越州會稽人。

translations.literal: Kang Ziyuan was a native of Kuaiji in Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Ziyuan was a native of Kuaiji in Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 仕歷獻陵令。

translations.literal: He served successively as Magistrate of Xianling.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Magistrate of Xianling.

sentences.zh: 子元擢累秘書少監，會真四門博士，俄皆兼集賢侍講學士。

translations.literal: Ziyuan was promoted in succession to Vice Director of the Secretariat; Huizhen became Simen Erudite; soon both also served as Lecturing Scholars at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyuan was promoted in succession to Vice Director of the Secretariat; Huizhen became Simen Erudite; soon both also served as Lecturing Scholars at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 玄宗將東之太山，說引子元、行果、徐堅、韋縚商裁封禪儀。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong was about to travel east to Mount Tai; Yue summoned Ziyuan, Xingguo, Xu Jian, and Wei Tao to discuss and revise the feng and shan ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong was about to travel east to Mount Tai; Yue summoned Ziyuan, Xingguo, Xu Jian, and Wei Tao to discuss and revise the feng and shan ritual.

sentences.zh: 初，高宗之封，中書令許敬宗議：「周人尚臭，故前祭而燔柴。」

translations.literal: Initially at Emperor Gaozong's feng, Chief Secretariat Director Xu Jingzong proposed: The Zhou people valued fragrance, therefore they sacrificed first and then burned the firewood.
translations.idiomatic: Initially at Emperor Gaozong's feng, Chief Secretariat Director Xu Jingzong proposed: "The Zhou people valued fragrance, therefore they sacrificed first and then burned the firewood."

sentences.zh: 說、堅、子元白奏：「《周官》：樂六變，天神降。

translations.literal: Yue, Jian, and Ziyuan submitted jointly: The Offices of Zhou: with six changes of music the heavenly spirits descend.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, Jian, and Ziyuan submitted jointly: "The Offices of Zhou: with six changes of music the heavenly spirits descend.

sentences.zh: 是降神以樂，非緣燔也。

translations.literal: Thus spirits descend through music—it is not because of burning.
translations.idiomatic: Thus spirits descend through music—it is not because of burning.

sentences.zh: 宋、齊以來，皆先嚌福酒，乃燎。

translations.literal: From Song and Qi onward all first tasted the blessing wine, then burned.
translations.idiomatic: From Song and Qi onward all first tasted the blessing wine, then burned.

sentences.zh: 請先祭後燔，如《貞觀禮》便。」

translations.literal: I request sacrificing first then burning, as in the Zhenguan Rites.
translations.idiomatic: I request sacrificing first then burning, as in the Zhenguan Rites."

sentences.zh: 行果與趙冬曦議，以為：「先燎降神，尚矣。

translations.literal: Xingguo together with Zhao Dongxi debated that: Burning first to bring down the spirits is long established.
translations.idiomatic: Xingguo together with Zhao Dongxi debated that: "Burning first to bring down the spirits is long established.

sentences.zh: 若祭已而燔，神無由降。」

translations.literal: If one sacrifices and then burns, the spirits have no means to descend.
translations.idiomatic: If one sacrifices and then burns, the spirits have no means to descend."

sentences.zh: 子元議挺不徙。

translations.literal: Ziyuan's argument stood firm and did not shift.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyuan's argument stood firm and did not shift.

sentences.zh: 說曰：「康子獨出蒙輪，以當一隊邪？」

translations.literal: Yue said: Does Kang Zi alone break the chariot axle to face a whole squad?
translations.idiomatic: Yue said: "Does Kang Zi alone break the chariot axle to face a whole squad?"

sentences.zh: 議未判，說請決於帝，帝詔後燔。

translations.literal: The debate was undecided; Yue requested the emperor decide, and the emperor ordered burning afterward.
translations.idiomatic: The debate was undecided; Yue requested the emperor decide, and the emperor ordered burning afterward.

sentences.zh: 乘輿自岱還，減從官，先次東都，唯子元、毋煚、韋述以學士從。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned from Dai, the retinue of officials was reduced; the emperor first stopped at the Eastern Capital, with only Ziyuan, Wu Jiong, and Wei Shu following as scholars.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage returned from Dai, the retinue of officials was reduced; the emperor first stopped at the Eastern Capital, with only Ziyuan, Wu Jiong, and Wei Shu following as scholars.

sentences.zh: 久乃徙宗正少卿，以疾授秘書監，致仕。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan; due to illness he was appointed Director of the Secretariat and retired.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan; due to illness he was appointed Director of the Secretariat and retired.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈汴州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously appointed Prefect of Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Prefect of Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗制贊賜說、子元，命工圖其象，詔冬曦、述、煚分為傳。

translations.literal: The emperor once composed encomia to bestow on Yue and Ziyuan, ordered artisans to paint their images, and commanded Dongxi, Shu, and Jiong each to write a biography.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once composed encomia to bestow on Yue and Ziyuan, ordered artisans to paint their images, and commanded Dongxi, Shu, and Jiong each to write a biography.

sentences.zh: 侯行果

translations.literal: Hou Xingguo
translations.idiomatic: Hou Xingguo

sentences.zh: 行果者，上谷人，歷國子司業，侍皇太子讀。

translations.literal: Xingguo was a native of Shanggu; he served successively as Vice Director of the Directorate of Education and attended the crown prince's lectures.
translations.idiomatic: Xingguo was a native of Shanggu; he served successively as Vice Director of the Directorate of Education and attended the crown prince's lectures.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈慶王傅。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously appointed Tutor to the Prince of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Tutor to the Prince of Qing.

sentences.zh: 始，行果、會真及長樂馮朝隱同進講。

translations.literal: Initially Xingguo, Huizhen, and Feng Chaoyin of Changle entered together to lecture.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Xingguo, Huizhen, and Feng Chaoyin of Changle entered together to lecture.

sentences.zh: 朝隱能推索《老》、《莊》秘義，會真亦善《老子》，每啟篇，先薰盥乃讀。

translations.literal: Chaoyin could investigate the hidden meaning of Laozi and Zhuangzi; Huizhen was also skilled in Laozi; each time they opened a chapter they first burned incense and bathed before reading.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyin could investigate the hidden meaning of Laozi and Zhuangzi; Huizhen was also skilled in Laozi; each time they opened a chapter they first burned incense and bathed before reading.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我欲更求善《易》者，然無賢行果雲。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: I wish to seek further those skilled in the Changes, yet there is none equal to the worthy Xingguo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I wish to seek further those skilled in the Changes, yet there is none equal to the worthy Xingguo."

sentences.zh: 朝隱終太子右諭德，會真太學博士。

translations.literal: Chaoyin ended as Right Mentor to the Heir Apparent; Huizhen as Erudite of the Grand Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyin ended as Right Mentor to the Heir Apparent; Huizhen as Erudite of the Grand Academy.

sentences.zh: 趙冬曦

translations.literal: Zhao Dongxi
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Dongxi

sentences.zh: 趙冬曦，定州鼓城人。

translations.literal: Zhao Dongxi was a native of Gucheng in Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Dongxi was a native of Gucheng in Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 進士擢第，歷左拾遺。

translations.literal: Selected by the jinshi examination, he served successively as Left Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Selected by the jinshi examination, he served successively as Left Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，上書曰：「古律條目千餘。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he submitted a memorial: Ancient statutes had more than a thousand articles.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shenlong he submitted a memorial: "Ancient statutes had more than a thousand articles.

sentences.zh: 隋時奸臣侮法，著律曰：『律無正條者，出罪舉重以明輕，入罪舉輕以明重。』

translations.literal: During Sui treacherous ministers mocked the law and wrote in the code: Where the code has no explicit article, for acquittal cite the heavier to clarify the lighter; for conviction cite the lighter to clarify the heavier.
translations.idiomatic: During Sui treacherous ministers mocked the law and wrote in the code: 'Where the code has no explicit article, for acquittal cite the heavier to clarify the lighter; for conviction cite the lighter to clarify the heavier.

sentences.zh: 一辭而廢條目數百。

translations.literal: One phrase abolished several hundred articles.
translations.idiomatic: One phrase abolished several hundred articles.

sentences.zh: 自是輕重沿愛憎，被罰者不知其然，使賈誼見之，慟哭必矣。

translations.literal: From this severity and leniency followed affection and hatred; the punished did not know why—if Jia Yi saw this he would surely weep bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: From this severity and leniency followed affection and hatred; the punished did not know why—if Jia Yi saw this he would surely weep bitterly.

sentences.zh: 夫法易知，則下不敢犯而遠機阱；

translations.literal: When law is easy to know, those below dare not violate and keep far from traps.
translations.idiomatic: When law is easy to know, those below dare not violate and keep far from traps;

sentences.zh: 文義深，則吏乘便而朋附盛。

translations.literal: When text and meaning are deep, clerks take advantage and partisan attachment flourishes.
translations.idiomatic: when text and meaning are deep, clerks take advantage and partisan attachment flourishes.

sentences.zh: 律、令、格、式，謂宜刊定科條，直書其事。

translations.literal: Statutes, commands, regulations, and forms—I say articles should be revised and set forth, stating matters directly.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes, commands, regulations, and forms—I say articles should be revised and set forth, stating matters directly.

sentences.zh: 其以準加減比附、量情及舉輕以明重、不應為之類，皆勿用。

translations.literal: Categories such as increase and decrease by comparison, measuring circumstances, citing the lighter to clarify the heavier, and what ought not to be done—all should not be used.
translations.idiomatic: Categories such as increase and decrease by comparison, measuring circumstances, citing the lighter to clarify the heavier, and what ought not to be done—all should not be used.

sentences.zh: 使愚夫愚婦相率而遠罪，犯者雖貴必坐。

translations.literal: Let foolish men and foolish women together keep far from crime; offenders though noble must be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Let foolish men and foolish women together keep far from crime; offenders though noble must be punished.

sentences.zh: 律明則人信，法一則主尊。」

translations.literal: When statutes are clear people trust; when law is unified the lord is honored.
translations.idiomatic: When statutes are clear people trust; when law is unified the lord is honored."

sentences.zh: 當時稱是。

translations.literal: At the time this was praised as correct.
translations.idiomatic: At the time this was praised as correct.

sentences.zh: 開元初，遷監察御史，坐事流岳州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he was transferred to Investigating Censor and was banished to Yuezhou for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he was transferred to Investigating Censor and was banished to Yuezhou for an offense.

sentences.zh: 召還復官，與秘書少監賀知章、校書郎孫季良、大理評事鹹廙業入集賢院脩撰。

translations.literal: Recalled and restored to office, he entered the Hall of Assembled Worthies as Compiler together with Vice Director of the Secretariat He Zhizhang, Proofreader Sun Jiliang, and Case Reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review Xian Yiye.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled and restored to office, he entered the Hall of Assembled Worthies as Compiler together with Vice Director of the Secretariat He Zhizhang, Proofreader Sun Jiliang, and Case Reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review Xian Yiye.

sentences.zh: 是時，將仕郎王嗣琳、四門助教範仙廈為校勘，翰林供奉呂向、東方顥為校理。

translations.literal: At that time Candidate Gentleman Wang Silin and Simen Assistant Instructor Fan Xianxia served as collators; Hanlin Attendant Lü Xiang and Dongfang Hao served as proofreaders.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Candidate Gentleman Wang Silin and Simen Assistant Instructor Fan Xianxia served as collators; Hanlin Attendant Lü Xiang and Dongfang Hao served as proofreaders.

sentences.zh: 未幾，冬曦知史官事，遷考功員外郎。

translations.literal: Before long Dongxi took charge of historiographical affairs and was transferred to Assistant Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Dongxi took charge of historiographical affairs and was transferred to Assistant Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 逾年，與季良、廙業、知章、呂向皆為直學士。

translations.literal: After more than a year he together with Jiliang, Yiye, Zhizhang, and Lü Xiang all became Direct Erudites.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he together with Jiliang, Yiye, Zhizhang, and Lü Xiang all became Direct Erudites.

sentences.zh: 冬曦俄遷中書舍人內供奉，以國子祭酒卒。

translations.literal: Dongxi was soon transferred to Secretariat Drafter with inner palace appointment and died while serving as Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Dongxi was soon transferred to Secretariat Drafter with inner palace appointment and died while serving as Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 冬曦性放達，不屑世事。

translations.literal: Dongxi was by nature free and unrestrained, disdaining worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Dongxi was by nature free and unrestrained, disdaining worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 兄夏日，弟和璧、安貞、居貞、頤貞、匯貞，皆擢進士第。

translations.literal: Elder brother Xiar, younger brothers Hebi, Anzhen, Juzhen, Yizhen, and Huizhen—all were selected in the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother Xiar, younger brothers Hebi, Anzhen, Juzhen, Yizhen, and Huizhen—all were selected in the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 安貞給事中，居貞吳郡采訪使，頤貞安西都護。

translations.literal: Anzhen was Attendant Within the Gates; Juzhen was Regional Inspector of Wujun; Yizhen was Protector-General of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhen was Attendant Within the Gates; Juzhen was Regional Inspector of Wujun; Yizhen was Protector-General of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 居貞子昌，別傳。

translations.literal: Juzhen's son Chang has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Juzhen's son Chang has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 王嗣琳以太子校書郎罷。

translations.literal: Wang Silin was dismissed from his post as Proofreader to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Silin was dismissed from his post as Proofreader to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 東方顥上書忤旨，左遷高安丞。

translations.literal: Dongfang Hao submitted a memorial that offended the intent and was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Gao'an.
translations.idiomatic: Dongfang Hao submitted a memorial that offended the intent and was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Gao'an.

sentences.zh: 廙業亦坐事左遷余杭令。

translations.literal: Yiye was also demoted for an offense to Magistrate of Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: Yiye was also demoted for an offense to Magistrate of Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 仙廈善講論，後為道士。

translations.literal: Xianxia was skilled in discourse and later became a Daoist priest.
translations.idiomatic: Xianxia was skilled in discourse and later became a Daoist priest.

sentences.zh: 開元集賢學士，又有尹愔、陸堅、鄭欽說、盧僎名稍著。

translations.literal: Among Kaiyuan erudites of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, Yin Yin, Lu Jian, Zheng Qinshuo, and Lu Zuan also achieved some renown.
translations.idiomatic: Among Kaiyuan erudites of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, Yin Yin, Lu Jian, Zheng Qinshuo, and Lu Zuan also achieved some renown.

sentences.zh: 尹愔，秦州天水人。

translations.literal: Yin Yin was a native of Tianshui in Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yin was a native of Tianshui in Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 父思貞，字季弱。

translations.literal: His father Sizhen, courtesy name Jiruo.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sizhen, courtesy name Jiruo.

sentences.zh: 明《春秋》，擢高第。

translations.literal: He mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals and was selected with high rank.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals and was selected with high rank.

sentences.zh: 嘗受學於國子博士王道珪，稱之曰：「吾門人多矣，尹子叵測也。」

translations.literal: He once studied under Erudite of the Directorate of Education Wang Daogui, who praised him saying: Among my disciples there are many, but Young Yin cannot be fathomed.
translations.idiomatic: He once studied under Erudite of the Directorate of Education Wang Daogui, who praised him saying: "Among my disciples there are many, but Young Yin cannot be fathomed."

sentences.zh: 以親喪哀毀。

translations.literal: He was destroyed by grief in mourning for a parent.
translations.idiomatic: He was destroyed by grief in mourning for a parent.

sentences.zh: 除喪，不仕。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he did not take office.

sentences.zh: 左右史張說、尹元凱薦為國子大成。

translations.literal: Left and Right Historiographers Zhang Yue and Yin Yuankai recommended him as Great Completion Scholar of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Historiographers Zhang Yue and Yin Yuankai recommended him as Great Completion Scholar of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 每釋奠，講辨三教，聽者皆得所未聞。

translations.literal: At each libation sacrifice he lectured and debated the Three Teachings; listeners all gained what they had never heard.
translations.idiomatic: At each libation sacrifice he lectured and debated the Three Teachings; listeners all gained what they had never heard.

sentences.zh: 遷四門助教，撰《諸經義樞》、《續史記》皆未就。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Simen Assistant Instructor and compiled Hubs of Interpretations of the Classics and Continuation of the Records of the Historian—both unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Simen Assistant Instructor and compiled Hubs of Interpretations of the Classics and Continuation of the Records of the Historian—both unfinished.

sentences.zh: 夢天官、麟臺交辟，寤而會親族敘訣，二日卒，年四十。

translations.literal: He dreamed that the Directorate of the Imperial Clan and the Directorate of the Imperial Library both summoned him; waking, he gathered kin to bid farewell and died two days later at age forty.
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed that the Directorate of the Imperial Clan and the Directorate of the Imperial Library both summoned him; waking, he gathered kin to bid farewell and died two days later at age forty.

sentences.zh: 愔博學，尤通老子書。

translations.literal: Yin was broadly learned and especially versed in Laozi's book.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was broadly learned and especially versed in Laozi's book.

sentences.zh: 初為道士，玄宗尚玄言，有薦愔者，召對，喜甚，厚禮之，拜諫議大夫、集賢院學士，兼脩國史，固辭不起。

translations.literal: Initially a Daoist priest, when Emperor Xuanzong valued arcane discourse someone recommended Yin; summoned for audience the emperor was greatly pleased, treated him generously, and appointed him Remonstrance Grand Master and Erudite of the Hall of Assembled Worthies concurrently compiling the national history—he firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Initially a Daoist priest, when Emperor Xuanzong valued arcane discourse someone recommended Yin; summoned for audience the emperor was greatly pleased, treated him generously, and appointed him Remonstrance Grand Master and Erudite of the Hall of Assembled Worthies concurrently compiling the national history—he firmly declined and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 有詔以道士服視事，乃就職，顓領集賢、史館圖書。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to attend to duties in Daoist garb; only then did he take office and exclusively supervised the books of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and the Historiographical Institute.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to attend to duties in Daoist garb; only then did he take office and exclusively supervised the books of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and the Historiographical Institute.

sentences.zh: 開元末，卒，贈左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyuan he died and was posthumously appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Horse.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Kaiyuan he died and was posthumously appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Horse.

sentences.zh: 陸堅，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Lu Jian was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jian was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 初為汝州參軍，以友婿李慈伏誅，貶涪州參軍，再遷通事舍人。

translations.literal: Initially Assistant in Ruzhou, he was demoted to Assistant in Fuzhou when his friend by marriage Li Ci was executed, and was transferred again to Master of Communications.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Assistant in Ruzhou, he was demoted to Assistant in Fuzhou when his friend by marriage Li Ci was executed, and was transferred again to Master of Communications.

sentences.zh: 有詔起復，遣中官敦諭，不就。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to resume office from mourning; palace envoys were sent to urge him, but he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to resume office from mourning; palace envoys were sent to urge him, but he would not accept.

sentences.zh: 以給事中兼學士。

translations.literal: He served as Attendant Within the Gates concurrently as Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attendant Within the Gates concurrently as Erudite.

sentences.zh: 善書。

translations.literal: He was skilled in calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 初名友悌，玄宗嘉其剛正，更賜名。

translations.literal: His original name was Youti; the emperor praised his upright firmness and bestowed a new name.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Youti; the emperor praised his upright firmness and bestowed a new name.

sentences.zh: 從封泰山，封建安男。

translations.literal: Following the feng at Mount Tai he was enfeoffed as Baron of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Following the feng at Mount Tai he was enfeoffed as Baron of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 帝待之甚厚，圖形禁中，親制贊。

translations.literal: The emperor treated him very generously, painted his image within the palace, and personally composed an encomium.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated him very generously, painted his image within the palace, and personally composed an encomium.

sentences.zh: 以秘書監卒，年七十一，贈吏部尚書，謚曰懿。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Director of the Secretariat at age seventy-one, posthumously appointed Minister of Personnel with posthumous title Resolute.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Director of the Secretariat at age seventy-one, posthumously appointed Minister of Personnel with posthumous title Resolute.

sentences.zh: 鄭欽說

translations.literal: Zheng Qinshuo
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Qinshuo

sentences.zh: 鄭欽說，後魏濮陽太守敬叔八世孫。

translations.literal: Qinshuo was eighth-generation descendant of Jingshu, Administrator of Puyang in Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Qinshuo was eighth-generation descendant of Jingshu, Administrator of Puyang in Later Wei.

sentences.zh: 開元初，繇新津丞請試五經，擢第，授鞏縣尉、集賢院校理。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan from Assistant Magistrate of Xinjin he requested trial examination in the Five Classics, was selected, and appointed Magistrate of Gong and Proofreader at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaiyuan from Assistant Magistrate of Xinjin he requested trial examination in the Five Classics, was selected, and appointed Magistrate of Gong and Proofreader at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 歷右補闕內供奉。

translations.literal: He served successively as Right Supplementation Censor with inner palace appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Right Supplementation Censor with inner palace appointment.

sentences.zh: 通歷術，博物。

translations.literal: He mastered calendrical arts and was broadly learned in things.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered calendrical arts and was broadly learned in things.

sentences.zh: 初，梁太常任昉大同四年七月於鐘山壙中得銘曰：「龜言土，蓍言水，甸服黃鐘啟靈址。

translations.literal: Initially Liang Director of Imperial Sacrifices Ren Fang in the seventh month of Datong year 4 at Zhongshan obtained an inscription reading: Tortoise speaks of earth, milfoil speaks of water; the thousand-li domain and yellow bell open the numinous site.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Liang Director of Imperial Sacrifices Ren Fang in the seventh month of Datong year 4 at Zhongshan obtained an inscription reading: "Tortoise speaks of earth, milfoil speaks of water; the thousand-li domain and yellow bell open the numinous site.

sentences.zh: 瘞在三上庚，墮遇七中己。

translations.literal: Burial on the third upper geng; collapse meeting the seventh middle ji.
translations.idiomatic: Burial on the third upper geng; collapse meeting the seventh middle ji.

sentences.zh: 六千三百浹辰交，二九重三四百圮。」

translations.literal: Six thousand three hundred successive cycles intersect; two nines doubled three four hundred collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Six thousand three hundred successive cycles intersect; two nines doubled three four hundred collapse."

sentences.zh: 當時莫能辨者，因藏之，戒諸子曰：「世世以銘訪通人，有知之者，吾死無恨。」
